I call it the winter to which the Gospel referred, saying: “But pray ye that your flight be not in the winter” (Mt 24:20). And in winter the flourishing qualities of virtue are extinguished.

The queen was right when she commanded by her authority that the north wind be driven far away. And she called upon the warm wind of midday, which she calls the south wind, by which a flood-stream of joy overflows: “Come, thou south; blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out.” She likens it to the mighty wind that blew in the upper room when the disciples were in it (Acts 2:2): “And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them.” As though they were living plants, this wind helps the garden of God to produce fragrant herbs, and sends forth prophecies from which sweet odors rise, and the commandments of salvation for the faith by the mouth of the Apostles, and the perfume of their teachings goes forth in all languages. This south wind made the teachings of the hundred and twenty... who were growing in the house of the Lord overflow upon all the nations of the earth (Acts 1:15).

The bride now says to the south wind, “blow upon my garden,” because her bridegroom made her a mother of gardens: the text includes gardens and a fountain. For this reason the Bridegroom desires for His garden, the Church, which is filled with living trees, that this wind blow upon it, to carry from it the fragrance of its perfumes. And the prophet says: “stormy wind fulfilling his word” (Ps 148:8). The bride adorned herself with the splendid adornment of the queen, and changed the streams that overflow with perfume into something more beautiful, making them flow from the trees of the gardens by the power of the Holy Spirit. By this image we can learn the difference between the Old and New Testaments: the river of prophecy is full of water, while the rivers of the Gospel are full of perfume. And the river of St. Paul carried the sweet fragrance of Christ, and overflowed from the garden of the Church by the Holy Spirit. The other examples, John, Luke, Matthew, Mark and all the other Apostles, all signify noble plants in the garden of the bride, and when it blows upon them at the midpoint of noon the south wind becomes, altogether, springs of perfumes for the sweet fragrance of the Gospels.
St. Gregory of Nyssa By the breath of God frost (ice) is given: and the breadth of the waters is straitened [10].

The falling of ice (frozen water) is permitted. Although the appearance of ice results from natural causes, even these phenomena do not occur at random, but God is the Controller of nature. The Psalmist says: “He giveth snow like wool: he scattereth the hoarfrost like ashes. He casteth forth his ice (his snow) like morsels: who can stand before his cold?” (Ps 147:16-17).

* Who is it who pours out the air in such great abundance...? He does not supply it by measures according to the rank of men and their wealth, nor is it bounded by certain limits, nor does He divide it according to the ages of the people, but as He used to distribute the manna (Ex 16:18), He supplies enough for all equally; and the winged chariot of creation, and the seat of the winds, and the intermediate seasons of the year, and the Giver of life to living beings, or rather the Preserver of the natural life of the body, by which bodies live and by which they speak, and in which is the light and all that shines upon it, and the sight that pours forth through it...? What are the storehouses of the winds? What are the treasures of the snow...? And as Scripture says: Who begot the drops of dew? From whose womb came the snow? And who binds the water in the clouds, and fixes the parts of the clouds...

* [When God breathes, the ice is frozen] [10]. When the Holy Spirit breathes on the hearts of believers and grants the wonders of great power, the flesh grows that causes paralysis (numbness) in the dullness of the hearts of unbelievers. The unbelieving multitudes become hardened against God by the very causes that make the humble people cease from the stubbornness to which they were bound. For when God breathes on them, those became ice, as they said through their envy of the miracles He wrought: “behold, the world is gone after him” (Jn 12:19). They saw the signs, and recognized the miracles wrought by His servants, and had already seen the whole world go to follow the preaching of the faith. Yet the more the Holy Spirit filled the world, the more they clung to the malice of envy that binds their minds.

[And He pours out the water in abundance]. For the Lord truly pours out the waters in abundance after this ice. After He bore the hardness of the Jews, after His death, He at once melted their hearts from the hardness of their unbelief, breathing upon them the breath of love toward Him, so that they ran to Him eagerly to obey Him, as far as possible, as the wise man says: [As the ice in fair weather, so shall your sins melt away and be taken from you] (see Sir 3:17)...

Of the waters, that is, the people gathered together toward the Lord, it is said: “He sendeth out his word, and melteth them: he causeth his wind (his breath) to blow, and the waters flow” (Ps 147:18).

Was not Paul ice as he was going to Damascus, after he had received letters, and was working against the seeds of the word of God that had been scattered in the hearts of believers as in the earth, so that they might not sprout and reach the perfection of good works? But this ice was turned to water, and was afterwards watered by the streams of holy counsels, those whom he had formerly sought to press down by persecution. This was so that they might bring a plentiful harvest for the elect, to the extent that God’s rains from the mouth of the persecutor watered them.
St. Gregory of Nazianzus Also by watering he wearieth the thick cloud.
he scattereth the cloud of his light [11].
When the Lord waters the earth He empties the thick cloud so that it pours rain on the earth, that it may sprout and buds may appear. In the Septuagint: “The wheat asks for a cloud.”

“He scattereth the cloud of his light.” Some see that God in His love makes the dense clouds like a pregnant woman who suffers pain as she gives birth to a child. The dense clouds bring rains and are dispersed, as though they bear pains for the service of man and the watering of the earth for him.
When the rains fall, the clouds become light and bright.
And it is turned round about by his counsels: that they may do whatsoever he commandeth them upon the face of the world in the earth [12].

The clouds seem to revolve upon themselves at random. God moves the clouds according to His pleasure, and they obey Him and go from one place to another on the face of the earth. The clouds have no ability to move as they please, but the will of the Creator is carried out.

If the movements of the clouds need divine guidance, how much more does mankind need this guidance. The wise man says: “Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety” (Prov 11:14). “Every purpose is established by counsel: and with good advice make war” (Prov 20:18).
The Psalmist tells us of the submission of nature with all its phenomena to God, saying: “Fire, and hail; snow, and vapours; stormy wind fulfilling his word” (Ps 148:8).
Whether it be for correction, or for his land, or for mercy, he causeth it to come [13].

The movements of nature, such as the clouds laden with rain that seem random, are by God’s permission, either for correction, or as a sign of God’s favor toward man, or out of His tenderness and mercy upon him.
He sometimes permits storms and floods for correction, as happened in the ancient world (Gen 7:11-12).

“For his land”: when God sends rain on the earth as a sign of His favor and delight in man, He regards the earth as His own land. The Psalmist says: “The earth is the LORD’S, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein” (Ps 24:1).

The text in the Vulgate reads: “Whether in one tribe, or in his land, or in whatever land, according to His mercy He sends it.” If the storms and the clouds full of rain move according to His pleasure, He also determines for them the place where they blow or fall.

By saying “for his land” God wishes to affirm that He longs for man to live as in the Lord’s land, as though He raises from him another Adam dwelling in the garden of God, which He plants with His hands and waters with the waters of His grace, to bear joyful and delightful fruits for the godly man.

entries.section: 3. Job, a judge unqualified to judge God’s providence

paragraphs.text: 14 “Hearken unto this, O Job: stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God. 15 Dost thou know God’s attention to them, or the shining of the light of his cloud? 16 Dost thou know the balancings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him which is perfect in knowledge? 17 How thy garments are warm, when he quieteth the earth by the south wind? 18 Hast thou with him spread out the sky, which is strong, and as a molten looking glass? 19 Teach us what we shall say unto him; for we cannot order our speech by reason of darkness. 20 Shall it be told him that I speak? if a man speak, surely he shall be swallowed up. 21 And now men see not the bright light which is in the sky: but the wind passeth, and cleanseth it. 22 Out of the north cometh gold: with God is terrible majesty.”
Hearken unto this, O Job: stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God [14].

Elihu invites Job to turn his gaze from the afflictions that have come upon him and driven him to murmur, and to consider earnestly the wondrous works of God and His surpassing works for believers. By this his mind and heart are filled with love for God and he perceives His divine care, and his soul finds rest within him. The Psalmist says: “The works of the LORD are great, sought out of all them that have pleasure therein” (Ps 111:2).

entries.section: 3. Job, a judge unqualified to judge God’s providence

paragraphs.text: Dost thou know God’s attention to them, or the shining of the light of his cloud [15].
Elihu asks: Can man grasp how God moves the storms, clouds, rains and so on, and how He brings forth shining lightning from dark, gloomy clouds?

entries.section: 3. Job, a judge unqualified to judge God’s providence

paragraphs.text: Dost thou know the balancings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him which is perfect in knowledge [16].

Who knows how the clouds are suspended in the air in a wonderful balance, how they are formed from evaporated water and gather together in the air, and remain floating in a certain place for a certain time, as though a hidden hand held and kept them, and then fall as rains to water the earth. They reveal a great and perfect wisdom!
With all that science and knowledge have attained, we can account for these phenomena, but they are not under man’s authority, and he is unable to grasp all their secrets exactly.

entries.section: 3. Job, a judge unqualified to judge God’s providence

paragraphs.text: How thy garments are warm, when he quieteth the earth by the south wind [17].
How does man explain that his body becomes warm when the warm south winds blow, and even the clothes become warm?
We saw in the Song of Songs how the bride asks that the north wind and also the south wind blow upon her, so that her inner garden gives forth the joyful fruits of the Spirit (Song 4:16).
Some see that Elihu puts this question in a sarcastic way, for it is among the simplest things that clothes become warm when warm winds blow, yet man offers no exact explanation of this phenomenon.

entries.section: 3. Job, a judge unqualified to judge God’s providence

paragraphs.text: Hast thou with him spread out the sky, which is strong, and as a molten looking glass? [18]
He asks him: Did you spread out with God the strong sky of heaven like a molten mirror? Were you with God when He made the breadth of the winds and their extent in proportion to their weight?
Do you not see how the heaven, when it is clear, is like a huge, strong molten mirror?

Here he speaks of the sky of heaven as a mirror. Scripture also speaks of it as like a tent or a curtain: “It is he that stretcheth out the heavens as a curtain (as a veil), and spreadeth them out as a tent to dwell in” (Isa 40:22). And also as a scroll: “And the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll: and all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree” (Isa 34:4). And sometimes as a garment: [The heavens are the work of thy hands. They shall perish, but thou shalt endure: yea, all of them shall wax old like a garment; as a vesture shalt thou change them, and they shall be changed] (Ps 102:25-26).
“Strong,” so that it supports itself by itself.
Teach us what we shall say unto him;

entries.section: 3. Job, a judge unqualified to judge God’s providence

paragraphs.text: for we cannot order our speech by reason of darkness! [19]

Elihu invites Job to pay attention to the thunder, which symbolizes the voice of God and expresses the greatness of God. In humility Elihu declares that man’s mind is exceedingly dark, unable to enter into dispute with the great God, and if he does so let him expect his destruction [19-20].
Since Elihu feels great awe toward God, he asks Job to teach him what to say to the awesome God, what words he can utter in the face of God’s greatness.

Job often repeated his plea to enter into a trial with God and to touch the divine presence in order to complain to Him of his condition. So Elihu advises him not to ask this, for the words will flee from his lips when he stands before the majesty of the great God.

It is as though he says to him: “You seem to be very wise, and to have complete knowledge about God; grant us to be wise like you, so that we may be able to approach God and speak with Him, for we feel as though we were wrapped in darkness. For our part we confess our ignorance and helplessness; tell us and teach us how to stand to argue with Him!” Or it is as though he says to him: “Men cannot explain God’s wonders and grasp their secrets, and so we cannot enter into a quarrel with Him. Teach us how we can do this?”
Shall it be told him that I speak?

entries.section: 3. Job, a judge unqualified to judge God’s providence

paragraphs.text: if a man speak, surely he shall be swallowed up [20].

He says: Can I dare to whisper in the presence of God? And if someone should speak against me and accuse me before Him because of what I have said, even if he made the accusation with sincere intent, how could I dare to stand in His presence? For I would be swallowed up by terror, and perish at the loftiness of His majesty.
If anyone dares to speak what does not befit the majesty of God, that is, if he is a murmurer, he is utterly swallowed up!

entries.section: 3. Job, a judge unqualified to judge God’s providence

paragraphs.text: And now men see not the bright light which is in the sky: but the wind passeth, and cleanseth it [21].

If God’s greatness is now hidden, it will surely be suddenly revealed at some time in the fullness of its splendor, when the darkness is scattered from Job’s eyes. This is as happens with the sun, whose rays are hidden behind the cloud, but as soon as the winds blow and scatter the clouds its splendor appears.

So it is fitting for the believer whose eyes are veiled by trials from seeing the splendor of God’s glory, His righteousness and His justice, to wait in patience and longsuffering, for the Holy Spirit will blow upon him, removing from him the cloud of darkness, and he will see what had been hidden from his eyes.

Since the storm had indeed begun, Elihu asks Job to wait patiently, for the time was near when God would reveal Himself to him in His splendor and speak with him, after the winds drive away the cloud of trials that darkened his eyes.

Some see that Elihu here refers to man’s inability to see the sun in its splendor once the winds blow and the sky becomes clear of clouds; how then can he ask to see God face to face to present his complaint before Him? Instead it is fitting for him to bow down before Him, submitting to Him in a spirit of humility, instead of murmuring and speaking with God as one who accuses Him.
God declares Himself as a passing cloud that leaves the light of the sun very bright, which can be seen in the splendor of His glory that surrounds us [21-22].
Out of the north cometh gold:

entries.section: 3. Job, a judge unqualified to judge God’s providence

paragraphs.text: with God is terrible majesty [22].
In the Septuagint: “The clouds shine like gold.”
When Elihu saw the storm coming from the north, he explained that the clouds coming with the storm flash like pure, shining gold as a symbol of God’s approach.

St. Augustine sees that the north points to the city of the Gentiles, while Zion is in the south, and that the devil ruled the north, where he says: “I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God: I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north” (Isa 14:12-13). When the Gentiles accept faith in the Lord Christ, they leave the kingdom of the devil and are freed from it, and they come from the north, having become gold, that is, having become kings, enlightened by grace in Christ Jesus; they have become a golden cloud.

entries.section: 4. God is perfect, great and awesome

paragraphs.text: 23 “Touching the Almighty, we cannot find him out: he is great in power, and in judgment, and in plenty of justice: he will not answer. 24 Men do therefore fear him: he regardeth not any that are wise of heart.”
Touching the Almighty, we cannot find him out:
he is great in power, and in judgment, and in plenty of justice.
He will not answer [23].

Even if God draws near to Job through a visible splendor surrounded by clouds and storms and sits on a throne of polished gold, yet, in Elihu’s opinion, it is impossible for anyone to grasp God, for His greatness is exceedingly surpassing, His power is unlimited, and so are His justice and His righteousness. And it is fitting for Job to know beforehand that God’s appearing to him does not mean that He will answer his questions, for it is not the right of the creature to interrogate God, since it is unable to grasp His wisdom.
Men do therefore fear him:

entries.section: 4. God is perfect, great and awesome

paragraphs.text: he regardeth not any that are wise of heart [24].
It is fitting for men, when they meet God, to confess that they are sinners, ignorant and wretched, fearing the Holy and Wise One alone.

God does not show favor to a man as one who is wise in his own eyes, for what wisdom can be ascribed to any man when compared with God, who is all-wise and all-knowing? What goodness can be ascribed to him when compared with the One alone who is holy?

Thus Elihu concludes his speech in a manner entirely different from the three friends. He concludes it by highlighting God’s greatness, majesty, wisdom and power, before which it is fitting for every man, whatever his ability and gifts, to submit in contrition.

He concluded his speech by saying that he sees the divine majesty drawing near to meet Job like a cloud of bright, polished gold, and he wants Job to prepare for this meeting by ceasing from murmuring and complaint, and by confessing God’s great works, His justice and His righteousness.
Elihu sees that the Lord is coming, and it is fitting that all human speech and dispute cease, that all submit in silence and listen to the divine voice.
It is enough for us to be convinced that He acts with justice [23-24].
May Your voice thunder in my heart!
* Let the storm of Your love blow in my depths, and let Your voice thunder in my heart!
No one can change my depths except the voice of Your love.
And no one gives me Your awesome fear, filled with sweetness, except Your voice.
The thunder of Your voice shakes my whole being. It shatters all corruption within me, and separates my soul from all temporal concerns.
In sweet awe my mind is lifted to the throne of Your grace, and my intellect is absorbed in Your majesty!
I long never to part from You until I depart from this world.
* The thunder of Your voice breaks the lofty cedars, and uproots from me all pride.
The clouds of Your love rain on the earth of my heart, and turn it into a joyful heavenly garden.
It bears the surpassing fruits of the Spirit.
* In the midst of this dense cloud You flash suddenly.
I see the rays of Your lights for moments, and my soul is enlightened by You, and I come to know Your secrets.
Your light cools every darkness in me, and turns my darkness into radiant light!
* The waters of the rains turn into dazzling white snow.
My heart, covered by the snow, becomes utterly pure!
My soul praises You, for You scatter my sins and take them away, and my soul is filled with the snow of Your radiant wisdom.
* The enemy of good, the ravenous beast, makes every effort to break into Your garden in me.
He will not be able to come near as long as You are within me.
And if he deceives me and enters, he will not settle, for Your grace drives him out quickly!
Yes, keep Your garden from this wicked enemy!
* Let the warm south wind blow upon Your garden, that my soul may be filled with the warmth of the Spirit.
And my heart may burn with Your holy zeal!
If You permit the cold north wind to blow upon me; if You permit trials to surround me, I am confident in the riches of Your love and wisdom.
You who move nature in all its greatness for my sake, how can I not trust Your good ordering of my whole life?!

entries.section: 1. God challenges Job to answer His questions

paragraphs.text: 1 Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said, 2 "Who is this that darkeneth counsel by words without knowledge? 3 Gird up now thy loins like a man; for I will demand of thee, and answer thou me.
Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said [1]:

Some see that the Hebrew word translated here "whirlwind" differs from the one used for the storm in the previous chapter. In the previous chapter it points to a state of agitation, turbulence, uproar and violent upheaval, whereas here it points merely to a storm that fills Job's mind with a sense of awe and reverence for the greatness of God. As God spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai amid thunder and lightning (Ex 19:16-19), so He spoke with Job as a sign of the greatness of His majesty (Ps 18:9-13; Hab 3:3-6; Ps 50:3-4).

Although God appeared to Job in order to commend and justify him before those present, yet without partiality He revealed to him his weaknesses, and wished to remove from him his murmuring and complaint. For in God's tenderness toward man, He gives him countless blessings after He directs him so that his errors and weaknesses may be removed from him.

* When Job lost all his wealth, when he lost his children, everything began to work against him. But since he loved the Lord, all the evils that befell him worked for his good (Job 42:9-17). What befell his body prepared him for the crown of heaven (Job 7:5). Before the time of trial God had never spoken with him as a friend with his friend (Job 38:1; 42:9). So let the catastrophe come, let trials fall, as long as Christ comes after the calamity!

St. Jerome * What then of Him who answered Job out of the whirlwind and the cloud, slow to chastise and swift to help, who does not allow the rod of sinners to rest upon the lot of the wicked (Ps 3:25) lest the righteous learn evil?
St. Gregory of Nazianzus Someone may ask: Why did God speak with Job through the whirlwind?

First: He feared for Job lest he fall into pride because of the praise that He would give him publicly, since He asks his friends not only to apologize to him but even to ask him to pray for them. Therefore God wished to preserve Job's life and his victories with a spirit of humility.

Second: God spoke with Job through the whirlwind and not through angels, as happened with some saints such as Daniel the prophet, or through visions as happened with Ezekiel the prophet, or through dreams as happened with Joseph the righteous, in order to rebuke Job's friends, declaring the honor of this righteous man, that the Lord Himself should come down to him to enter into dialogue with him, a thing for which they themselves had not been made worthy.
Third: St. John Chrysostom sees that God covered Job with clouds and storms like one who has come to speak with him from the mercy seat that is upon the lid of the ark of the covenant (Num 7:89).

* In my opinion, (God) arranged at that moment that a cloud should cover the righteous man in order to lift up his thoughts and to persuade him that this voice was coming from on high, as in the case of the mercy seat that was upon the ark of the testimony (Num 7:89). For as the cloud is a symbol of heaven, so it is as if God wished to place heaven itself upon Job, and came with His throne drawing near to him. It seems to me that this same thing happened on the mountain when a thick cloud settled there (Ex 19:16), that we might understand that the voice came from on high.

St. John Chrysostom Perhaps some ask why the Lord began by rebuking Job and putting to him questions that reveal his weakness in grasping the mysteries of God, His wisdom and His plan, although He had praised him before Satan and had also defended him before his friends. This is God's surpassing love for His believers: though He sometimes stands firm with them even in the midst of their afflictions and trials, yet He defends them before others and prepares for them surpassing glories. He fears for them lest they fall by the sword of pride, but His eyes are upon them; He keeps them, sanctifies them, and glorifies them before His angels and men, and even before Satan.

* After the loss of his possessions, the death of his children, the wounds of his body, his wife's words urging him toward evil, the language of abuse directed at him by his comforters, and the arrows of many sorrows that he received with courage, it was fitting that the blessed Job be praised by the Judge for such great strength of endurance, since the time was near for his being called out of this present world.

Now the time has come for him to receive double and to regain his former health, so that he might enjoy for a long time the possessions restored to him. Therefore God rebukes with firm justice the one whom He had kept alive, lest through his very victory he perish by the sword of pride.
Pope Gregory (the Great)

entries.section: 1. God challenges Job to answer His questions

paragraphs.text: "Who is this that darkeneth counsel by words without knowledge?" [2]

It was fitting for Job to shed light on the wisdom of God so that others might come to know it, but instead he spoke of the injustice that had befallen him. Thus God corrects the position of Job, who, although righteous, uttered some words of reproach and so distorted the picture of God's plan before those present.

God reproaches him, saying to him: Who are you, who wish to speak about the deep mysteries of God, His justice and His providence? For since you do not comprehend them, you offer a dark interpretation of them.

The text in the Septuagint reads: [Who is he that hides counsel from me, and who shuts up words in his heart and thinks to conceal them from me?] The Jesuit translation reads: "Who is this that darkens my justification with words that are nothing of knowledge?" St. Cyril the Great used this expression in his commentary on the Gospel of Luke (Lk 22:64): "And when they had covered him (blindfolded his eyes), they struck him on the face, and asked him, saying, Prophesy, who is it that smote thee?"

* He says in a certain place through one of His holy prophets: [Who is he that hides counsel from me, and who shuts up words in his heart?] (Job 2:38) He who searches the hearts and minds and is the giver of all prophecy, how could He not know who smote Him (Lk 64:22)? As Christ says: [Darkness has blinded their eyes; and their minds have become blind] (cf. Jn 12:40).

entries.section: 1. God challenges Job to answer His questions

paragraphs.text: St. Cyril the Great * God points to the vast distance that separates us from Him. {Tell me: who is it that tries to hide himself from me, I who know the secrets exactly?!} St. John Chrysostom Gird up now thy loins like a man; for I will demand of thee, and answer thou me [3].
While God appeared in the whirlwind, before which no man can stand, He asks Job to gird himself like one preparing himself for a work of the utmost gravity (Ex 11:12; 1 Kgs 46:18).

The word "man" גֶבֶר here in Hebrew, geber, means a hero. It is as if God says to him: Put away from your mind all fears, and stand courageously as a hero before me. I will present to you a series of questions; when you answer them, you will be answering yourself concerning the questions that you used to set out before your friends about me.

As for His saying "gird up... thy loins," or gird yourself: since garments were loose in ancient times, a man had to gird himself in order to run, to work, or to enter battle. To this day most soldiers and commanders gird themselves during war.
* When Job fell into a state of discouragement, God turned him back from it with these words.

* Girding is part of the soul's journey. Hear what God says to that righteous man: "Gird up now thy loins like a man; for I will demand of thee, and answer thou me" (Job 3:38). He says this also to all the prophets. He tells Moses to gird himself. He Himself appeared to Ezekiel (Ezek 11:9) LXX girded. No, and the angels also appear to us girded (Rev 6:15), as soldiers. When we gird ourselves, we also stand courageously, and by our standing we gird ourselves.

St. John Chrysostom * The Lord also commanded Job to gird himself, as if it were a kind of sign of maturity (manhood) and readiness for work. He said to Job: [Gird up thy loins like a man] (Job 38:3).

St. Basil the Great * In this too St. David boasts that he is girded with the strength of God (Ps 32:18), and he speaks of God Himself as clothed with strength (Ps 1:93), and as girding Himself with His power - against the wicked - although some prefer to see in this a declaration of the abundance of His power, as though it appeared restrained, since He covers Himself with light as with a garment (Ps 2:104). For who can bear His unlimited power and His light?
St. Gregory of Nazianzus

entries.section: 2. Job's ignorance of how the earth was created

paragraphs.text: 4 Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding. 5 Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest? or who hath stretched the line upon it? 6 Whereupon are the foundations thereof fastened? or who laid the corner stone thereof; 7 When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth?
Declare, if thou hast understanding [4].

The first question God puts to him touches the very existence of his own being, as He asks him where he was when God laid the foundations of the earth for his sake. On the one hand, neither Job nor even Adam himself had yet been created; on the other hand, God created the earth for him and for his brothers before they had any existence.

Job was not in existence when God founded the earth, and therefore he had no ability to work with God in creation, or to offer counsel, or even to perceive and understand what God was doing for his sake. How then does he dare to complain of God's plan toward him? If Job is unable to understand the laying of the earth's foundations, can he comprehend God's plan and wisdom?

* God says: What are you saying? For your sake I founded the earth with such care, would I then neglect him for whose sake I created it...? He utters this to those who demand that He give an account and explanation of events without looking to the loftiness of His wisdom. Who urged me to this? Who advised me? Who came to help me?
St. John Chrysostom Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest?

entries.section: 2. Job's ignorance of how the earth was created

paragraphs.text: Or who hath stretched the line upon it? [5]

He asks him: If you know, who set the measures of the earth and determined the dimensions of the equator? Who is the architect who designed the dimensions of the earth? Who held the line to measure it, defining its regions and dimensions?

The divine discourse stresses that the earth on which man lives did not come into being by chance without planning, but behind it stands the supreme Architect who laid down a precise plan for its construction; it was created by the wisdom of the Creator and His surpassing power.
* The measures were not taken without creativity, nor did it come about by chance or in a random manner, but God designed it with a harmonious purpose, working as a skillful architect.

St. John Chrysostom Pope Gregory (the Great) offers us a symbolic interpretation of this phrase, seeing that this earth is the life of man, and that the foundation on which our life stands is firm faith in the fear of the Lord. This faith, with all its measures, is the work of God in us; we may not ascribe it to ourselves.

* The foundation of this earth is faith. The foundation of this earth is laid when the hidden places of the heart are marked by the fear of God as the first cause of stability... It is said to Job: Do not ascribe to yourself the virtues that you received from me... So that I may not destroy in you what I have built, you ought not to cease meditating on the state in which I placed you... For we can keep well what we are if we never ignore what we were...

Who lays the foundations of this earth but our Creator? He who by the hidden ordering of His inner plan gives to one the word of wisdom, to another the word of knowledge, to another perfect faith, to another the grace of healing, to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another discerning of spirits, to another divers kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of sermons... Thus does our Creator and the Orderer of all things act, to keep us from being puffed up by the gift that a person receives, and that he may be humbled by the virtues he has not received... God governs all things thus, so that all receive particular gifts, and all are counted the property of each person individually, through the bond of love. Each one possesses in the other what he himself lacks, and in humility offers to the other what he has received as his own possession. As Peter says: "As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God" (1 Pet 4:10)... And Paul says: "By love serve one another" (Gal 5:13)... And also: "As God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith" (Rom 12:3).
Pope Gregory (the Great)

"Who hath stretched the line upon it?" Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that those who stretch the line upon the earth to instill the spirit of faith are the preachers, those who cannot work except by God Himself. He gave as an example the Apostle Paul, who neglected to preach in Macedonia, and a man of Macedonia appeared to him in a vision, that he should go and help them (Acts 16:9). And when the Apostle tried to go to Bithynia, he was prevented (Acts 16:7).

entries.section: 2. Job's ignorance of how the earth was created

paragraphs.text: Whereupon are the foundations thereof fastened? or who laid the corner stone thereof [6]?

The discourse here is symbolic, speaking of the creation of the earth as a palace that God built for man the king, digging its foundations and laying a corner stone for the erection of an integral building, strong and exceedingly wide.

If the Lord Christ, the incarnate Word of God, or faith in Him, is the foundation on which the new earth, the Church of God, stands, then its bases or the pillars that stand on this foundation are the holy life in the Lord, or the virtues that we practice by the righteousness and grace of Christ, whereby our hearts, our will and all our inner powers are sanctified.
Since Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that the holy earth the Lord founded is faith, what then are the bases of this earth?
* What do we understand by the bases of this earth other than the teachers of the holy Church...?

The bases may also refer to the prophets, for when they first spoke plainly of the incarnation of the Lord we saw them as bases resting on the foundation (perhaps he means the Lord Christ, the foundation of faith) and bearing the building that stands upon them...

"Or who laid the corner stone thereof?"... It is clear to all who is He whom Scripture calls the corner stone. Truly it is He who took into Himself the Jews on one side and the Gentile people on the other, and united them together as two walls in the building of the Church. It is written, "hath made both one" (Eph 2:14). He showed Himself as the corner stone not only in the lower things but also in the upper, for He united the peoples of the Gentiles with the people of Israel on earth, and united both together with the angels in heaven. For the angels proclaimed at His birth: "On earth peace" (Lk 2:14).
Pope Gregory (the Great)
"Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain: and he shall bring forth the corner stone among those who shout, Honor, honor to it" (Zech 4:7).
"Built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone" (Eph 2:20).

St. Augustine sees that by calling the Lord Christ the head of the corner, who is the head of the Church, the Church thus becomes the corner that joined the Jews on one side and the Gentiles on the other.

* It happened on that day which is called His birth that the Jewish shepherds saw Him, while on this day, which should be called "the Divine Manifestation," that is, "the Revelation," the Gentile Magi worshiped Him... Truly He was born as the corner stone for the two, and as the Apostle says: "For to make in himself of twain one new man, so making peace; And that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross" (Eph 2:15-16). What is a corner stone but the joining of two walls of different directions, as though they were exchanging a kiss! The circumcised with the uncircumcised, that is, the Jews with the Gentiles, who bore a common enmity, and had fundamental matters that separated them from one another, for the Jews worshiped the one true God, and the Gentiles worshiped many false gods. The former were near and the latter were far. He led both parties to Himself, He who reconciled them to God in the one body, and as the same Apostle said: and that by the cross, slaying the enmity.

entries.section: 2. Job's ignorance of how the earth was created

paragraphs.text: St. Augustine When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy? [7]
When building a house or a church or some project, a person celebrates with his friends the beginning of digging the foundations and the beginning of laying them.

At the beginning of the rebuilding of the Temple [they set the priests in their apparel with trumpets, and the Levites the sons of Asaph with cymbals, to praise the Lord, and they sang together by course in praising and giving thanks unto the Lord; because he is good, for his mercy endureth for ever toward Israel. And all the people shouted with a great shout, when they praised the Lord, because the foundation of the house of the Lord was laid] (Ezra 3:10-11). And as the Lord establishes His Church, it is said: "the corner stone shall come forth among those who shout, Honor, honor to it" (Zech 4:7). At the birth of the Lord Christ, the corner stone of the Church of the New Testament, "suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host praising God" (Lk 2:13).

What a wonderful picture, as the luminous heavenly orders, the "morning stars," went forth shouting and praising God when they saw the foundations of the earth being laid. Although it was not laid for them, but for man who was to come, and not for them, in love they counted man's happiness their own happiness, and what is offered to him as though it were theirs.
God likens Himself to an architect who built a wonderful house, when He created the world, and the heavenly orders rejoiced at this surpassing work. Where was Job at that time?

In the seventh chapter of the Conference of Abba Serenus he made clear that God created the heavenly beings before He created the world. "When the stars were made together, the angels praised me with a loud voice" (Job 7:38) LXX. The angels were thus present at the beginning of the creation of the world, praising Him for His works in creating the visible world for us.

In a comment by St. John Chrysostom on the signs of the end found in (Mt 29:24), he says that the angels praised the Lord with a loud voice when He created the stars (cf. Job 38:7) LXX. All the more will they praise Him when the final change takes place and the stars fall, since they will no longer be needed, for there is no night in eternity.

* All the glorious, unutterable harmony of the heavenly beings above, whether in the service of God or in the common agreement among the heavenly powers, can be preserved by the guidance of the Spirit.

St. Basil the Great * Who dares to suppose that the angels were created after the six days of creation? If he is so foolish, his foolishness is removed by Scripture, which has similar authority, where God says: [When I made the stars, the angels shouted to me with a loud voice] (Job 38:7). If the angels existed before the stars - and the stars were created on the fourth day - shall we then say that the angels were created on the third day? God forbid! For we know what was created on that day. The dry land was separated from the waters, every element took its distinctive form, and the earth brought forth everything upon it.
St. Augustine

entries.section: 3. His ignorance of setting boundaries for the seas

paragraphs.text: 8 "Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it brake forth, as if it had issued out of the womb? 9 When I made the cloud the garment thereof, and the mist a swaddlingband for it, 10 And brake up for it my decreed place, and set bars and doors, 11 And said, Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further: and here shall thy proud waves be stayed?"
Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it brake forth, as if it had issued out of the womb [8]?
Perhaps he refers here to the third day of creation when God said: "Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place" (Gen 1:9).
The earth and the deep were mixed together, and when God commanded their separation the waters rushed forth as from the womb of the earth and the seas were formed.
The vast seas were formed and became as though shut in with doors or gates from which they do not go out.
Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that the sea here symbolizes the heart, which man cannot guard or sanctify without divine grace.

* What is this sea but our heart, raging in a violent, bitter struggle, swelling with the haughtiness of pride, and darkened with the deceit of evil? How great is the power of its raging waves, a thing understood by him who understands in himself the mystery of the trials of thoughts.
Pope Gregory (the Great)

* Why does it say "it issued out of the womb" (when it was born)? To show that this took place in stages, and that creation did not come about as by one stroke. It reflects for the hearer what Moses said. As though it had been born, the sea first poured forth, and afterwards took its form and was gathered together into one place (Gen 1:9). So do not think it natural for the sea to be bounded by its shores; rather, God at first allowed the contrary, that the water should exist and spread over the whole surface of the earth.
St. John Chrysostom God set boundaries for the primeval sea.

entries.section: 3. His ignorance of setting boundaries for the seas

paragraphs.text: When I made the cloud the garment thereof, and the mist a swaddlingband for it [9].

As He looks at the sea as a newborn child needing clothes and swaddling, God gave it the clouds as a garment covering it, and the mist as a swaddling band to wrap it. Thus God deals with the vast sea as with a little child who needs a nurse to swaddle it and care for it, in spite of its violently raging waves and its sweeping currents.
He did not say that He made the mountains and rocks and hills its swaddling band, but He made the mist so, a thing that would never occur to the mind of man.
* Do not think that the mist over the waters is a natural thing. He says that it exists by His (divine) command.

entries.section: 3. His ignorance of setting boundaries for the seas

paragraphs.text: St. John Chrysostom And brake up for it my decreed place, and set bars and doors [10].
Lest the sea rage and rebel and destroy man's life on the earth, God bound it by certain limits, and set up for it bars and doors to put limits to its movement.

These limits, bars and doors were not set to make the sea lose its ability to fulfill its role or to destroy its mission, but on the contrary, they are for the benefit of the sea itself as well as for the benefit of the earth.

God sets for our hearts a divine law or commandment, not to stifle us, nor to deprive us of happiness and freedom, but by this divine commandment we are shaped and return to become in the image of God and to be like Him. This is for our happiness and the happiness of others.

The commandment does not confine us as in a prison, but helps our hearts to be enlarged with love toward God and men, even those who oppose us, and we even love all creation, and love our own souls in the Lord.

entries.section: 3. His ignorance of setting boundaries for the seas

paragraphs.text: And said, Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further: and here shall thy proud waves be stayed? [11]

We do not find here anything of the myths that spread anciently, such as the appearance of huge, terrifying sea creatures. Rather, in a wonderful literary and spiritual style, it depicts the sea as though it were born in an atmosphere of calm, having its vital role in interacting with the dry land to serve man. Despite the vastness of the ocean and the violence of the deeps, God set laws that it does not transgress.

* Who can tell of the depths of the seas, their vastness and the power of their mighty waves?! And yet they stand at the limits set for them, for it is said: [Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further, and here thou shalt enter, and here shall thy proud waves be stayed]. So the sea clearly shows obedience, for it runs and stands at the shore in a clear line made by the waves, declaring to those who look upon it that it does not transgress the limits set for it.

St. Cyril of Jerusalem Jeremiah the prophet says: "Fear ye not me? saith the LORD: will ye not tremble at my presence, which have placed the sand for the bound of the sea by a perpetual decree, that it cannot pass it: and though the waves thereof toss themselves, yet can they not prevail; though they roar, yet can they not pass over it?" (Jer 5:22). Theodoret, bishop of Cyrus, presents the sea as proof of divine providence.

* To persuade you of this, return again to the sea, and observe its depth, its extent, its divisions into bays, its shores, its harbors, the islands in its midst, the kinds of fish in it, their species, forms and variety and their fondness for the shore. Observe the limits of its waves, and the bridle of providence that controls them and keeps them from flooding over the land. When the waves rush upon the sand they keep to the limits, observing the divine law engraved there. They resemble a spiritual horse restrained by its trainer: the waves bow their necks and recede, like one who offers repentance by drawing back when touching the sand.
Father Theodoret, bishop of Cyrus * Among the weakest of things is sand, yet the sea cannot resist it in its violence, for it is bridled by it.
St. Basil the Great

entries.section: 4. His ignorance of how the light of dawn emerges

paragraphs.text: 12 "Hast thou commanded the morning since thy days; and caused the dayspring to know his place; 13 That it might take hold of the ends of the earth, that the wicked might be shaken out of it? 14 It is turned as clay to the seal; and they stand as a garment. 15 And from the wicked their light is withholden, and the high arm shall be broken.
Hast thou commanded the morning since thy days?
Hast thou caused the dayspring to know his place [12]?

God presents Job with perplexing questions so that he may discover his total inability to comprehend the wisdom of God and feel that there is no basis of comparison between his thinking and God's thinking. These questions, although science, with the progress of research, provides answers to some of them, yet the mysteries of nature remain beyond all human thought. What we know scientifically cannot be compared with what we do not yet know.
Here he speaks of the first appearance of light at dawn; we are all certain of the existence of light and enjoy it with the dawn until the sun rises.

He did not ask him: Is it in your power to hasten the appearance of the dawn and the breaking forth of the light? Rather, he asked him about two matters: whether man was present when the Lord commanded the light to appear, and whether he can determine a place for the dawn. Man was not present when God created the light, and it is not in his power to command the light to shine, nor to determine the place on which it shines. As the psalmist says: "The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork" (Ps 19:1-2).
* The heavens (the celestial bodies) obey Him, as they move in peace in subjection to His laws.
Day and night they run the course appointed to them, without hindering one another.
The sun and the moon with the stars pass through the course appointed to them, according to His command, without any deviation.
And the fruitful earth, according to His will, brings forth in due seasons abundant food for man and beasts and all the living creatures that are on the face of creation...
The depths (the abyss) that cannot be fathomed, and the indescribable arrangements of the nether world, are subject to the same laws.
The sea, immeasurably vast, is gathered together by His work, and does not pass the bounds set for it, but complies with His commands.
For He said: [Hitherto shalt thou come, and thy waves shall be broken in thy depths] (Job 38:11).
An ocean that man cannot pass over, and worlds that lie beyond it are directed by the will of the Lord.
The seasons of spring, summer, autumn and winter succeed one another peacefully, the one after the other.

The winds perform their service at the appointed time without hindrance, and the unfailing springs offer their breasts without ceasing as life for men. The smallest of living things come together in concord and peace.

All these works the great Creator, Lord of the universe, has ordered, moving in harmony and concord, doing good to all, especially to us, who find refuge in His tenderness, through our Lord Jesus Christ.
To whom be glory and majesty for ever and ever. Amen.

Pope Gregory (the Great), in his symbolic interpretation, sees that the holy Church is called the dawn because she looks to the reward of the bright heavenly life and abandons the darkness of sin; she is enlightened by the rays of the Sun of righteousness.
That it might take hold of the ends of the earth (of the extremities of the earth), that the wicked might be shaken out of it? [13]

The dawn is pictured as appearing in the midst of darkness to shine with beautiful colors, so that the works of sinners, who find in the darkness of night an opportunity to practice their dark evils, cease.
Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that the extremities of the earth are the humble whom the Lord Christ takes hold of, that is, the fishermen who silence the teachers of the Law.
It is turned as clay to the seal; and they stand as a garment [14].

In Egypt, Babylon and Assyria bricks bore a stamp distinguishing the brickworks from one another. Egyptian wine jars and the places where mummies were placed were sealed with a seal on clay. In Assyria some public documents were found with clay stamped with certain letters, distinguishing the official seal. Also the chambers in which treasures were placed were sealed with a seal on clay. Perhaps the tomb of the Lord Christ was sealed thus (Mt 27:66). Clay was preferred to wax because the former grows harder by fire, while the latter melts by it.

With every new morning the sun rises on the earth, and it appears illumined as if wearing a new garment; thus the Sun of righteousness imprints His light on His Church, making her a new dawn, enjoying with every morning a new experience in the enjoyment of God's love for her. Thus the image of Christ appears on His Church and His true believers as the seal appears on clay.
And from the wicked their light is withholden, and the high arm shall be broken [15].

Job had previously spoken of the terror of thieves and criminals at the morning light because it exposes them (Job 24:13). Here God announces the rays of the morning light, that is, the rays of the Sun of righteousness who clothes the true Church with the bright garment of His righteousness, and at the same time deprives the wicked of the light of their joy, and breaks their arm which they lift up against God and men.

The light of the Lord Christ, which gives eternal life to His believers, is judgment to those who oppose Him. The Lord Christ Himself says: "If I had not come and spoken unto them, they had not had sin: but now they have no cloak for their sin" (Jn 15:22). And the Apostle Paul says: "To the one we are the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life" (2 Cor 2:16).

* To whom then is it "the savour of death unto death" but to those who do not believe, and who are not subject to the Word (Logos) of God...? Again, who are those who are saved and receive the inheritance? Without doubt they are those who believe God and continue in His love, as did Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun (Num 30:14) and the innocent children (Jonah 11:4) who have no sense of evil. But who are those who are saved now, and enjoy eternal life? Are they not those who love God, and believe His promises, and become children in malice (1 Cor 20:14)?
St. Irenaeus

entries.section: 5. His ignorance of perceiving the shadow of death and the darkness

paragraphs.text: 16 "Hast thou entered into the springs of the sea? or hast thou walked in the search of the depth? 17 Have the gates of death been opened unto thee? or hast thou seen the doors of the shadow of death? 18 Hast thou perceived the breadth of the earth? declare if thou knowest it all. 19 Where is the way where light dwelleth? and as for darkness, where is the place thereof, 20 That thou shouldest take it to the bound thereof, and that thou shouldest know the paths to the house thereof? 21 Knowest thou it, because thou wast then born? or because the number of thy days is great?
Hast thou entered into the springs of the sea? or hast thou walked in the search of the depth? [16]
He asks him whether he knows what lies hidden in the depth of the sea and the treasures it holds, and whether he can describe the springs of the sea's waters.
He returns to the primeval world, and shows the ocean, even if destructive, cooperating with death; so did Job comprehend the secrets of the waters and the secret of death?

* He points to Job's confusion: [and in the paths of the dawn (the depth) hast thou walked]. I tell you, not only can you not accomplish one of these works that I have made, but you cannot even know how they were accomplished, nor know or imagine them as they truly are. By these words He was teaching Job of the distance that separates Job and his sons.

entries.section: 5. His ignorance of perceiving the shadow of death and the darkness

paragraphs.text: St. John Chrysostom Have the gates of death been opened unto thee? or hast thou seen the doors of the shadow of death? [17]

Now that He has asked him about matters concerning nature itself, such as the appearing of the dawn, the springs of the sea, and what the sea beds contain, He asks him about a sure matter that touches man's life, namely death, which, as it is said of it, accompanies man from the moment of his birth, and he does not know when it will come upon him. Death remains a riddle in man's life; he does not know when it will come upon him, or by what means, nor can he describe it, nor describe the place to which his soul departs, nor how he lives after death. These are matters that faith offers us and the Creator, the Lover of mankind, reveals to us, although it is a reality that touches the life of every man!

Some see that by death he means the place where souls gather after their departure, that is, the kingdom of the dead, or Hades, while the shadow of death points to the very movement of the souls' exodus and departure. These are obscure matters for man, but they are open to God.

* Truly, how can we wonder if men have failed with their earthly wisdom to comprehend the mystery of God the Father and of our Lord Jesus Christ, in whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge (Col 3:2), this mystery that the angels could not have known without its being revealed to them!

For who can by himself - and not by faith - picture, following the Lord Jesus, how He (the Word) came down from the heights of heaven to the lowest parts of Hades, and behold, He ascends from Hades to the heavens, and at the same time dwells among us without lessening anything of what He was...

The angels also stood in marvelous astonishment before the heavenly mystery; thus when the Lord rose, the heights of heaven could not bear the glory of the resurrection from the dead of Him who had at last been confined in the narrow bonds of the tomb, so that the angels were in perplexity...!

For the "Conqueror" came adorned with astonishing spoils. The Lord came into His holy temple while angels and archangels went before Him, marveling at those spoils that were set free from death... And by the victory of the Cross - where the rule was upon His shoulders - the spoils were carried to an everlasting victory.

He came as though the gates had become too narrow for Him... for they cannot admit His greatness; therefore they sought wider ways and easier passages for the Lord in His return, and thus the Lord lost nothing by emptying Himself (since He returned to His heavenly glory with His spoils).

At any rate, they found that a new way must be prepared before the face of this new "Victor," for He is always, as He was, greater than others. But because the gates of righteousness, which are the gates of the Old and New Testaments, in which the heavens are opened, are everlasting gates, therefore they truly do not change, but were lifted up because the one entering is not a man, but the whole world enters in the person of the Savior of all.
St. Ambrose Hast thou perceived the breadth of the earth?

entries.section: 5. His ignorance of perceiving the shadow of death and the darkness

paragraphs.text: Declare if thou knowest it all! [18]

No one had yet gone around the globe, and no man up to that time could know its dimensions, although the earth itself is counted as a point in the midst of the greatness of the whole universe that God created.

entries.section: 5. His ignorance of perceiving the shadow of death and the darkness

paragraphs.text: Where is the way where light dwelleth? and as for darkness, where is the place thereof [19].
Light succeeds darkness, and darkness light; this is what man observes every day, but does he know the secret of light and the secret of darkness, where they dwell?

It is impossible for man to determine a specific place for tangible light and darkness; how then can he comprehend Him who created the light and separated it from the darkness? And what can man know of the light of divine righteousness and the darkness of evil?

What man knows is that God is able to turn the heart of man from the darkness of evil to the light of righteousness, but how this is accomplished, this he cannot describe precisely. Every day we touch this work of God, as He shines with the light of His righteousness upon sinners to turn sinners into saints.

entries.section: 5. His ignorance of perceiving the shadow of death and the darkness

paragraphs.text: That thou shouldest take it to the bound thereof, and that thou shouldest know the paths to the house thereof? [20]

Man often longs for the rising of the light of day to complete some work, as he longs for the darkness of night to rest from the toil of the day's work, but he does not know where the light of day or the darkness of night goes.

entries.section: 5. His ignorance of perceiving the shadow of death and the darkness

paragraphs.text: Knowest thou it, because thou wast then born? or because the number of thy days is great! [21]
God wished to show the truth about man apart from the sphere of His grace, so He asks Job whether he knows these things, whether his age goes back to the beginning of creation, and he was then born.

It is not fitting for man to argue with God about what exceeds his ability, such as the creation of light; rather, in faith he should listen to His divine word: [I form the light, and create darkness: I make peace, and create evil (chastisements): I the LORD do all these things] (Isa 45:7).

entries.section: 6. His ignorance of the clouds, the hail and the thunder...

paragraphs.text: 22 "Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow? or hast thou seen the treasures of the hail, 23 Which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war? 24 By what way is the light parted, which scattereth the east wind upon the earth? 25 Who hath divided a watercourse for the overflowing of waters, or a way for the lightning of thunder; 26 To cause it to rain on the earth, where no man is; on the wilderness, wherein there is no man; 27 To satisfy the desolate and waste ground; and to cause the bud of the tender herb to spring forth? 28 Hath the rain a father? or who hath begotten the drops of dew? 29 Out of whose womb came the ice? and the hoary frost of heaven, who hath gendered it? 30 The waters are hid as with a stone, and the face of the deep is frozen.
Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow?
Or hast thou seen the treasures of the hail [22]?

After God discussed the subject of creation, He pointed to existing natural phenomena such as the falling of snow, the blowing of winds and the falling of rain. All these God brought into being for the sake of every man. It was fitting for Job to contemplate these wonderful works, which human thought cannot completely define, and which exist for his sake, instead of being occupied with the trials that befall him. There is no basis of comparison between what God permits man of affliction and His divine providence over the whole world for man's sake. It befits the believer that his heart and mind be enlarged to glorify the Creator who ordains everything for his sake.
When snow falls in cold countries one is astonished at the countless quantities that fall on whole countries, so that it seems as though the storehouses of heaven had been filled with snow and hail.

The inhabitants of regions subject to snow feel God's care for them, and see in the snow precious treasures. For it keeps the earth's warmth so that its temperature does not fall many degrees below zero, and the snow gives fertility to the earth. Therefore, immediately after the snow period, we find the plants in the region that was covered with snow growing with wonderful speed.

The Lord uses snow and hail to accomplish His purposes, such as protecting His believers from the raids of the wicked, so He sends down upon them snow and hail on the day of battle, as happened at the time of the Flood when the waters poured out from these storehouses to drown the wicked world, and as He cast great stones from heaven upon the Canaanites (Josh 10:11).

Pope Gregory (the Great) sees in the snow and hail a reference to hearts that are cold in love toward God, as it is said: "the love of many shall wax cold" (Mt 24:12). These hearts the Lord looks upon not with disdain nor in a spirit of anger, but as treasures needing someone to move them. He Himself moved the heart of Saul of Tarsus, who confessed that he had been a blasphemer and a persecutor and a slanderer, and raised him up to be the great Apostle burning with holy zeal.

entries.section: 6. His ignorance of the clouds, the hail and the thunder...

paragraphs.text: Which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war? [23]
The Lord used these storehouses to chastise the wicked (Ex 9:18; Josh 10:11; Rev 16:21; Isa 28:17; Ps 18:12-13; Hag 2:17).

entries.section: 6. His ignorance of the clouds, the hail and the thunder...

paragraphs.text: By what way is the light parted, which scattereth the east wind upon the earth? [24]

In the phenomenon of thunderclouds the light of lightning appears for moments; but who can describe exactly how the light is emitted, and what its speed is, and what its substance is, and how it quickly dissipates, etc.?

Some see that he speaks of the light that issues with the dawn to spread over the earth. Such a phenomenon is simple, which men touch in their daily lives, and yet they do not comprehend its mysteries.

He also asks Job whether he understands how the east wind is distributed over the regions. Perhaps he linked light and the east wind in that their source is from the east, and they spread over regions and lands, and he cannot trace their spread.

entries.section: 6. His ignorance of the clouds, the hail and the thunder...

paragraphs.text: Who hath divided a watercourse for the overflowing of waters, or a way for the lightning of thunder [25].

It seems to man as though there were no restraint upon the rains, nor on the gathering of waters in branching channels, nor when the waters flood many lands as though they had departed from obedience to God who determined their course.
All things proceed by divine permission, and it is said of the king's heart that it is in the hand of God as the rivers of water, he turneth it whithersoever he will (Prov 21:1).
And as God directs the streams of water, so He has authority over the course of the lightnings.

entries.section: 6. His ignorance of the clouds, the hail and the thunder...

paragraphs.text: To cause it to rain on the earth, where no man is; on the wilderness, wherein there is no man [26].

If God determines even the places of the rain, then in His care for His creation He allows rain even in places not inhabited by people, so that the wild beasts may find water, or if a traveler passes through.

entries.section: 6. His ignorance of the clouds, the hail and the thunder...

paragraphs.text: To satisfy the desolate and waste ground; and to cause the bud of the tender herb to spring forth? [27]

Although God cares for man in a special way, He does not ignore the lowly creatures in the wildernesses, and the beasts of prey. As the psalmist says: "He sendeth the springs into the valleys, which run among the hills. They give drink to every beast of the field: the wild asses (the wild donkey) quench their thirst" (Ps 104:10-11).

entries.section: 6. His ignorance of the clouds, the hail and the thunder...

paragraphs.text: Hath the rain a father? or who hath begotten the drops of dew? [28]

He had previously spoken of the great sea as a child that came forth from the womb at God's command, swaddled by Him with mist and clothed with clouds, as though God were like a nurse even to the lifeless sea. Now he speaks of the dew, the uncounted drops, and portrays them as a newborn for whom God cares, even for a drop of dew! He is at work in all nature by His surpassing good nature.

St. John Chrysostom sees that God often uses the expression of birth even for lifeless creatures, to affirm that no creature came about by chance, but all things are in the mind of God, who is wholly love and care.
* [Who is the father of the rain?! And who hath begotten the drops of dew?!] (Job 38:28)

Who condensed the air into clouds, and bound them to carry the waters of the rains, so that they come golden in color (Job 37:22) from the south, in one order at one time, and in many circles and diverse shapes at another?!
"Who can number the clouds in wisdom?" (Job 38:37), for it is said in Job that He knows the parting of the clouds?! (Job 33:16) LXX.

Who is "he that bringeth forth the wind out of his treasuries" (Ps 135:7), and as we said before [Who begot the drops of dew, and out of whose womb came the snow?!] (Ps 135:7; Job 38:28), for its substance is water and its strength is like stone!
At one time the water becomes snow like wool (cf. Ps 16:147), at another He scatters it as hoarfrost like ashes, and at yet another it becomes a stony substance. He rules the water as He wills.

* The nature of water is one, but its work is manifold in power, for it works in the vine as wine that maketh glad the heart of man, and in the olive tree as oil to make his face to shine, and in bread strengthens man's heart (Ps 15:104), and it is found in all kinds of fruit that God created.
St. Cyril of Jerusalem Out of whose womb came the ice?

entries.section: 6. His ignorance of the clouds, the hail and the thunder...

paragraphs.text: The hoary frost of heaven, who hath gendered it? [29]

Waters freeze into ice and snow in an extremely short time and in quantities hard or impossible to count, revealing man's inability to comprehend natural phenomena that take place before him and with a speed he does not expect. What created power is able to accomplish these wonderful phenomena?
The waters are hid as with a stone.

entries.section: 6. His ignorance of the clouds, the hail and the thunder...

paragraphs.text: And the face of the deep is frozen [30].
Pope Gregory (the Great) grieves that the Jews, who used to be like the rains that water the earth, through their unbelief lost all spiritual warmth and became like cold, icy stones.

entries.section: 7. His ignorance of the stars and their effect on the earth

paragraphs.text: 31 "Canst thou bind the bands of the Pleiades, or loose the cords of Orion? 32 Canst thou bring forth the mansions in their seasons, and guide the Bier with its daughters? 33 Knowest thou the ordinances of heaven? canst thou set the dominion thereof in the earth?
Canst thou bind the bands of the Pleiades, or loose the cords of Orion? [31]

Since many philosophers linked the fates of men to the movements of the stars, he therefore spoke of the groups of stars, for God has created all these with wisdom, and however much man studies astronomy and comes to know some of the secrets of the stars, he has no authority over them, nor do the stars have any authority over the fates of men.

* Do you know who it is that numbers the stars and calls them by their names? Do you know the differences of glory that each of them has (1 Cor 41:15), and the order of their movement, that then I may trust you when you weave the fabric of human affairs and arm the creature against the Creator?

entries.section: 7. His ignorance of the stars and their effect on the earth

paragraphs.text: St. Gregory of Nazianzus Canst thou bring forth the mansions in their seasons, and guide the Bier with its daughters? [32]

By the mansions he means the stars that are in the south, and by the Bier the stars that are in the north. Who among men has authority to move the stars? But God alone uses them, as it is written in the book of Judges: "They fought from heaven; the stars in their courses fought against Sisera" (Judg 5:20).

The expressions "the mansions" and "the Bier" appear in the Septuagint as Mazuroth and the evening stars; and in the text of Pope Gregory (the Great), the morning star and the evening star. The Pope sees that the morning star is the Lord Christ, who announced to us the eternal morning, who rose in the morning from the dead and shone upon us with the splendor of His light, shattering the darkness of our corruption, so that John was right to call Him "the bright and morning star" (Rev 22:16). As for the coming evening star, it is the Antichrist, whom the Lord permits to rule over the sons of the earth, over the unbelieving hearts which accept the rule of the Antichrist over them.

* The Father brought the morning star in due time, for it is written: "But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, to redeem them that were under the law" (Gal 4:4-5). Being born of a virgin, He appeared as the morning star in the midst of the darkness of our night. For having driven away the gloom of sin, He announced to us the eternal morning. But He showed Himself as the morning star because He rose in the morning from the dead, and overcame by the splendor of His light the hideousness of the darkness of our death. Fittingly John called Him "the bright and morning star" (Rev 22:16), since He appeared alive after death. He became for us the morning star. He gave us life in His person, an example of the resurrection. As He also pointed to the coming (deceptive) light. He permits the evening star to dominate the sons of the earth in that He permits the Antichrist to dominate the unbelieving hearts of the Jews... The Lord says in the Gospel: "I am come in my Father's name, and ye receive me not: if another shall come in his own name, him ye will receive" (Jn 5:43). Paul also says: "Because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved. And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie: That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness" (2 Thess 2:10-12). Therefore the evening star will not dominate those who wished to be sons of heaven.
Pope Gregory (the Great)

entries.section: 7. His ignorance of the stars and their effect on the earth

paragraphs.text: Knowest thou the ordinances of heaven? canst thou set the dominion thereof in the earth? [33]

There is no one who knows the ordinances of heaven or comprehends its mysteries and decrees. But heaven comprehends what is on earth, and the heavenly beings discover much of the mysteries of God's love and His plan toward mankind. It is as if God says to Job: "If I have permitted trials for you, you do not know what goes on in heaven, but the heavenly beings know why I permitted you afflictions, and they know my love for you and my defense of you against Satan."

entries.section: 8. His ignorance of God's power in the sky and in natural phenomena

paragraphs.text: 34 Canst thou lift up thy voice to the clouds, that abundance of waters may cover thee? 35 Canst thou send lightnings, that they may go, and say unto thee, Here we are? 36 Who hath put wisdom in the dense cloud, or who hath shown understanding in the meteors? 37 Who can number the clouds in wisdom? or who can pour out the bottles of heaven, 38 When the dust is cast into a mass, and the clay (the clods) cleave fast together?
Canst thou lift up thy voice to the clouds, that abundance of waters may cover thee? [34]

We have already seen that the clouds refer to the prophets of the Old Testament and the apostles of the New Testament, for God speaks through His holy men as from the clouds, and He alone covers man with the waters of His grace and the gift of His Holy Spirit.

The Lord came speaking among the clouds, where the prophets bore witness to Him and the apostles preach Him, and the peoples have received faith in Him like many waters, as though the abundance of waters had covered Him. It was not possible for righteous Job, nor for any other man of the Old Testament, to comprehend this mystery clearly as it was realized by the coming of the Lord Christ.

entries.section: 8. His ignorance of God's power in the sky and in natural phenomena

paragraphs.text: Canst thou send lightnings, that they may go, and say unto thee, Here we are? [35]

The clouds refer to the apostles who went about preaching the Gospel, and the lightnings that issue from the clouds are the signs and wonders that God gave to the apostles to bear witness to the divine truth. One of these lightnings issuing from the clouds is what the Apostle Peter said to the lame man: "Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk" (Acts 3:6-7).
As the clouds are subject to God, so the lightning bears witness to Him in obedience.

entries.section: 8. His ignorance of God's power in the sky and in natural phenomena

paragraphs.text: Who hath put wisdom in the dense cloud, or who hath shown understanding in the meteors? [36]
Some translate the dense cloud as a hurricane. As for the meteors, they are a blazing flame of fire.
The Septuagint reads: "Who gives women skill in spinning (weaving) and knowledge of embroidery?"
* Note this: He speaks of the practical side. He mixes small things with great.

St. John Chrysostom St. Ambrose sees in this phrase a reference to the weaving of the heavenly breastplate of the Lord Christ as the Great High Priest, which is woven of the power of God and His wisdom and His righteousness, and adorned with precious stones. Or it is the heavenly wedding garment adorned with various stones and woven with gold; it is the fabric of working faith.

entries.section: 8. His ignorance of God's power in the sky and in natural phenomena

paragraphs.text: Who can number the clouds in wisdom? or who can pour out the bottles of heaven [37]?

"Bottles" translates the plural of the word "ziqq" (skin), that is, a flask. Can any man, however great his wisdom, number the clouds that are in the sky, and place them precisely, and determine their size and weight? And who can speak of the rains that pour from heaven as from huge flasks?

entries.section: 8. His ignorance of God's power in the sky and in natural phenomena

paragraphs.text: When the dust is cast into a mass, and the clay (the clods) cleave fast together? [38]

Although the wicked are like the chaff which the wind driveth away (Ps 1:4), or like the dust or dirt flying in the air, because they have no love uniting them together in the Spirit, yet God in His love gives them the spirit of love that they may cleave together like useful lumps of clay.

entries.section: 9. God's care for the irrational animals

paragraphs.text: 39 "Wilt thou hunt the prey for the lioness? or fill the appetite of the young lions, 40 When they couch in their dens, and abide in the covert to lie in wait? 41 Who provideth for the raven his food? when his young ones cry unto God, they wander for lack of meat?
Wilt thou hunt the prey for the lioness? or fill the appetite of the young lions [39]?

The choice of these animals and birds (Job 38:39 - 41:34) was not a choice without purpose, but it may be said that they represent the procession of animals and birds hostile to human society in man's view at that time. Therefore demons were often portrayed in the forms of these animals and birds. God's care is surpassing even for the beasts of prey and the birds that attack human society. For all of these, God not only knows their ways, but they are subject to Him and He sustains them.
