"Life" went down to him to meet him, and there shut the mouth of death, and then we are saved, saying: O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory? (1 Cor 15:55). The sting of death has been removed by Baptism! Here you are entering the waters carrying your sins, and by the invocation of grace, as we seal your souls, the terrifying beast will no longer swallow you.]
Can one take him before his eyes?
Or bore his nose with a snare? [24]

What is the snare that pierces the nose of the enemy of good? Pope Gregory (the Great) says: [What are they but the earnest counsels of the saints? They pierce the nostrils of this behemoth... The Lord pierces his nostrils with snares, when He takes away his strength, breaking the cunning of deception by the firm understandings of the saints].

How marvelous! God permits the existence of the devil, and does not take me from before him. For He knows that through Him I overcome him. I strike his arrogant nose with the spear of the Cross and I shatter it. By the Spirit of the Lord I live victorious and triumphant. I sing in the spirit of victory over Satan who fell from heaven like lightning!
* Satan aims arrows against me, but I have a sword with me.
He has a bow with him, but I am a soldier bearing heavy arms...
He is a bearer of the bow, but he does not dare to come near me, for he casts his arrows from afar.

*You lost Paradise, but God gave you heaven, so that He might confirm His tenderness, and that He defeats the devil, showing that even if he perfects tens of thousands of plots against the human race, they will not profit him, for God always leads us to a greater honor.
You lost Paradise (the garden of Eden), and God opened heaven to you.
You fell under the sentence of toil for a time, and you have been honored with life eternally.
God commands the earth to bring forth thorns and thistles, but the soil of the Spirit brings forth fruit for you. Do you not see that the gain is greater than the loss?
St. John Chrysostom * Paul tells them to be brave and strong like the wrestler and the soldier of Christ, doing everything with love for God and for one another.
St. Didymus the Blind * Let us put on our heads the helmet of salvation, so that we may not be wounded and die in the battle.
Let us gird our loins with truth, that we may not be found weak in the fight.
Let us arise and awaken Christ, and He will calm the waves for us.
Let us take the shield against the Evil One, as a preparation for the Gospel of our Savior (Eph 6:15-16).
Let us receive from our Lord the authority to reign over serpents and scorpions (Lk 10:19)...
Let us rejoice in our hope at all times (Rom 12:12), that He who is our hope and our Savior may rejoice in us...
Let us take for ourselves a weapon for the battle (Eph 6:16), which is the preparation of the Gospel.
Let us knock at the door of heaven (Mt 7:7), and it will be opened to us and we shall enter in.
Let us ask for mercy diligently, and we shall receive what is necessary for us.
Let us seek His kingdom and His righteousness (Mt 6:33).
Let us meditate on what is above, on the heavenly things, where Christ ascended and is glorified.
But let us forget the world which is not ours, until we reach the place to which we are called.
Let us lift up our eyes on high, to see the transfigured radiance.
Let us lift up our wings like eagles, to see where the carcase is (Mt 24:28)...

Our enemy is skillful, my dear, and the one who fights us is crafty. He prepares himself to attack the brave and victorious, to make them weak. But his own feeble ones he does not fight, for they are captives delivered up to him.
He who has two wings flies away from him with them, so that the arrows he hurls toward him do not reach him.
The spiritual see him fighting, and his weapon has no power over their bodies.

All the children of light do not fear him, for darkness flees from before the light. The children of the Good One do not fear the evil one, for He has given them to tread upon him with their feet (Gen 3:15).

St. Aphrahat * No sin arising from satanic affliction was able to approach the body of the Lord. The Lord stood firm against the enemy's temptations, in order to restore victory to mankind. He made Satan a plaything, as David proclaimed: "There is that leviathan, whom thou hast made to play therein" (Ps 104:26), and also: [He shall break in pieces the false accuser] (Ps 72:4). And also [Thou brakest the heads of leviathan in the waters] (Ps 74:13-14). And in the Book of Job the Lord declared that this leviathan would become a plaything and be caught in this trial, saying: "Canst thou draw out leviathan with an hook?" (Job 41:1).
Abba Chromatius
Who will rescue me from the devil but You?
* In the midst of my afflictions my soul is embittered.
I enter with You into bitter reproach.
I forget the truth about myself, that I am lowly dust before a great Creator.
* I have sinned in my thinking as in my words.
I spoke once and twice, I asked: Why do You prosper the way of the wicked?
Why do You permit afflictions to come upon me?
But I will proceed no further with words.
I am silent before You; Your arm is strong and Your voice thunders.
Your majesty and splendor, who can describe them? * I have discovered the truth of my weak self, and I have come to know the violence of the devil, my enemy.
Who will raise me up but You?
Who will deliver me from this enemy but You, O Lover of mankind?
* Strengthen me, that I may mortify my loins, and not allow the lusts of the flesh to destroy the desires of the Spirit.
The strength of the enemy is in his loins and the navel of his belly!
Keep me from him, and sanctify my loins and my belly.
* You created him a shining star, and in his wickedness he descended to Hades.
He wants to draw me down with him.
Who will deliver me from him but You?
He opens his mouth to swallow all the children of men.
Would that I might hide in You, so that he does not come near me.
May I enjoy Your Cross, and so pierce his nose.
May I live by Your Holy Spirit, and break his arrogant nose!

1 "Canst thou draw out leviathan with an hook? or press down his tongue with a cord? 2 Canst thou put a rope into his snout? or bore his jaw through with a hook? 3 Will he make many supplications unto thee? will he speak soft words unto thee? 4 Will he make a covenant with thee? wilt thou take him for a servant for ever? 5 Wilt thou play with him as with a bird? or wilt thou bind him for thy maidens? 6 Shall the company of fishers dig a pit for him? or shall they part him among the Canaanites? 7 Canst thou fill his skin with barbed irons? or his head with fish spears? 8 Lay thine hand upon him; remember the battle no more! 9 Behold, the hope of him is in vain: shall not one be cast down even at the sight of him? 10 None is so fierce that dare stir him up: who then is able to stand before me?
Canst thou draw out the crocodile with an hook, or press down his tongue with a cord? [1]

In God's discourse with Job about Satan, He wants to assure him that, with all his power and violence, he is, for the believer, nothing but something like a fish that can be caught with a small fishing rod.

Leviathan, by which Satan is meant here. Opinions about this name are many, of which we mention: 1. A huge water animal, violent and predatory. The Septuagint has Dralaonate, that is, dragon, as also in the Syriac and the old Arabic. The false prophet and the antichrist have been likened to the sea dragon and the land dragon [Rev 13]. 2. A deadly and unique kind of poisonous serpent. Some Jewish stories mention a huge serpent that coils around the whole earth, spewing its poisons. 3. A kind of deadly whale. 4. The crocodile of the river Nile is meant, as Bochart said. 5. Hasaeus holds that it is not a whale but the Orca, a water monster (a fearsome animal of strange shape), armed with sharp teeth, which terrifies the whales. 6. Grotius holds that it is a very huge fish called the mular or musar, found in the Mediterranean Sea. 7. Some, such as Schultens, hold that it is a symbolic name representing ancient terrifying animals, by which Satan is meant. 8. Pope Gregory (the Great) holds that his name may be called Leviathan as a kind of irony, since the word means something huge and dreadful.

Those who say that it is the crocodile rely on the following: 1. There are no whales in the Mediterranean or in the rivers of that region, but the crocodile is found in the river Nile and some rivers of Asia and Africa, so most likely Job had no knowledge of whales but of crocodiles. It is true that the Speaker is God and He knows all that He created, but He does not speak to Job of an animal that he had not heard of or known. 2. The characteristics given here of Leviathan apply to the crocodile, in that it is savage, violent and cannot be controlled. Its mouth is fearful and its size very great, armed with a huge row of teeth and covered with scales close together, and it is distinguished by its terrible eyes. It cannot be caught by the ordinary means of catching beasts of prey. (Its length is usually between 18 and 20 feet, but it sometimes reaches thirty feet.) The number of its very sharp teeth is 30 or more in each jaw. It is considered one of the most fearsome water animals. It often swims on the surface of the water to catch any animal it finds, and if it finds no food it approaches the bank and hides among the papyrus leaves, so that when any animal comes near to drink it pounces on it and drags it into the water to drown and eat it. It is famous for catching tigers that come to drink. 3. What supports the supposition that it is the crocodile is what is mentioned in Job 40:15 about behemoth, which is an animal of the water. Perhaps the two lived in the same region, for if behemoth is the sea horse or the behemoth or the sea giant, the hippopotamus, which was in the river Nile, then Leviathan is the crocodile found in the same river. Some drawings in Herculaneum show Egyptian landscapes in which we see the crocodile lying among the (water) reeds and the sea horse on the plants on an island. Also the famous mosaic in Praeneste represents the plants and animals of Egypt and Ethiopia. The sea horse and the crocodile are indicated together in one group on the Nile. Herodotus indicates that some Egyptians consider the crocodile sacred, while others attack it. Sometimes they treat it with excessive honor and offer it fish and precious foods, and adorn its head with earrings and its feet with bracelets and gold rings inlaid with precious stones. They tame it very gently, and after its death they embalm it with precious spices; this in regions such as Thebes and Owbite and Arsinoite and Maabdeh, opposite the present city of Manfalut. And in other regions they treated it with great disgust, and let no opportunity pass in which they could destroy it.
Gesenws holds that Leviathan is derived from Laowah (to twist), where one creature bends around another and coils around it, perhaps to destroy or devour it.

Herodotus mentions that among the ways of catching the crocodile, they put a piece of pork on a hook (a fishing rod) and throw it on the water to float, and then bring a live pig to the bank and beat it until it screams. The crocodile comes to the bank at the sound of its screaming to seize it, and when it finds the piece of meat it swallows it, and they pull it with the rod toward the bank, and the first thing they do to it is fill its eyes with mud so that they can control it.

The crocodile has no tongue, or has a very small tongue attached to the lower jaw; but just as in fishing the fish draws the hook with the bait through its tongue, so God asks whether Leviathan can be drawn by his tongue.

Thevenot holds that some used to dig pits on the bank and cover them with sticks, and when the crocodile falls into one of them it cannot get out. They leave it for several days without food, and then bind its jaw with ropes which they knot around it, and then drag it.
God directs our eyes to the enemy of all mankind: if it is hard to catch Leviathan with a hook and drag him out by his tongue with a cord, what will they do with the devil?

The devil is exceedingly violent and hard to overcome, but the Son of the living God came down to our earth, and when He became incarnate, this body of His, or His humanity, became the hook with which He catches him. The devil thought regarding Christ that, since He bore a body like all the children of men, and had a human soul, he had authority over Him, and could take Him into his kingdom of darkness. He stirred up his followers to crucify Him, reckoning this a victory over Him, and he did not realize the hook set for him, for by the Cross He put him to shame, deprived him of his authority, and drew out from him the captives who had fallen under his authority.

The Lord left the enemy of good and his followers to blaspheme Him and bring accusations against Him, and the enemy did not realize that by this he was being drawn by his tongue to go down to Gehenna, he and his angels who shared his blasphemy against the Savior of the world.

* Leviathan was caught with a fishing hook, when he was seized by the bait of the body of our Savior, for by the sharp prick of His divinity it pierced him at once. The hook caught him as in the throat of one who swallows it, when the bait of the body appeared to the devourer so that he might seize it at the time of His sufferings, and the divinity laid hold of him to kill him.

* Understand, O Job, what I do: when I send My only-begotten Son in the flesh to the death of the corrupter, in My Son the mortal body appears, while the power of His immortality does not appear. This is a kind of hook that destroys him who swallows it, by the hiding, with skill, of the power with which it wounds him.

"Or press down his tongue with a cord"... For sins are symbolized by the cord, as the prophet says: "Woe unto them that draw iniquity with cords of vanity" (Isa 5:18)... Also the "cord" expresses faith, as Solomon testifies, saying, "A threefold cord is not quickly broken" (Eccl 4:12). For the faith in the truth, which the mouth of those who preach the knowledge of the Trinity weaves, remains firm in the elect. It is broken only in the heart of the wicked. Here you may understand the word cord as faith or as sin. For our incarnate Lord bound the mouth of Leviathan with a cord, when He appeared in the likeness of sinful flesh and condemned all his sinful teachings... Through the likeness of sinful flesh the deceitful dialogue in the flesh was cooled, the tongue of Leviathan was bound, and when the truth was known, the false teachings fell silent.
Pope Gregory (the Great)

* Now, my beloved, Satan has been slain, that tyrant who is against the whole world... Death no longer reigns, but life rules instead of death, for the Lord says: "I am... the life" (Jn 14:6), so that everything is filled with joy and gladness, as it is written: [The LORD reigneth; let the earth rejoice] (a)... Now that death has been abolished and the kingdom of Satan has been destroyed, everything is filled with joy and gladness.

* If Satan, the enemy of our race, fell from heaven and turned to our lower realm, he has come to have authority over the spirits of his fellows, whom he uses as his followers, working by deceptions for the sake of disobedience. They work not only in those who are deceived, but they try to hinder those who rise upward, as the Apostle says: "According to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience" (Eph 2:2). The Lord came to drive Satan out and cleanse the air of him, preparing the way to heaven "through the veil, that is to say, his flesh" (Heb 10:20). As the Apostle says: What kind of death can accomplish this except the death that takes place in the air, I mean on the Cross...! It was very fitting for the Lord to endure this death, for by His being lifted up (on the Cross) He cleansed the air of the evil of the devil and of all kinds of demons, for He says: "I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven" (Lk 10:18); by this He made a new opening of the way to heaven, for He says also: [Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lift up, ye everlasting doors] [(Ps 24:7) Septuagint]. For the Word had no need of the opening of the gates, since He is the Lord of all, and none of His works is shut before Him; rather we are the ones who need the gates opened, since He bore us in His body. He offered death on our behalf, paving the way for us to the heavens.

* For the Lord touched every part of creation and freed it and set it free from all deceptions of falsehood and illusion, as St. Paul says, when He Himself spoiled principalities and powers, triumphing over them on the Cross. So that no one after Him should be deceived, but should find everywhere the Word of the true God.

St. Athanasius the Apostolic * The Lord stood firm against the trials that came from the enemy in order to restore the victory to mankind. By this He made Satan a plaything, as David proclaimed: [That leviathan, whom thou hast made to play therein] (Ps 104:26)... and also: [Thou brakest the heads of leviathan in pieces upon the waters] (Ps 73:13-14). The Lord declares in the Book of Job that this leviathan becomes a plaything and is caught in this trial: "Canst thou draw out leviathan with an hook?" (Job 41:1).

Abba Chromatius * Satan is deceived when he wounds himself with his own sting, and he fortifies against himself the one whom he thinks he is weakening. For the holy Job was fortified all the more when he wounded him, he who covered his whole body with sores, and he bore the stings of Satan and his poison did not affect him. Therefore it was well said to him: "Thou shalt draw out the dragon with a hook, and play with him as with a bird. Thou shalt bind him as a child does a sparrow, and lay thy hand upon him" (Job 41:1, 5, 8) LXX.

You see how Paul mocked him, as a child, as it is in the prophecy, put his hand on the hole of the serpent, and the snake did not hurt him. He drew him out of his hidden place, and made his poison a medicine, so that the poison for destroying the body became a medicine for healing the spirit. For what hurts the body benefits the spirit (1 Cor 5:5).

So let me allow the serpent to strike what is earthly in (my body); let me allow it to bite my flesh and cause it to turn livid, and the Lord will say of me: "Behold, he is in thine hand; but save his life" (Job 2:6).

What a power of God! He entrusts the keeping of man's soul to the hand of Satan, who wants his destruction...! By the Master's commandments He made Satan the keeper of His sheep, so that against his will he came to carry out the commandments of heaven, and by his harshness to obey the commandments of meekness!

* Such great distress and heavy grief came upon the demons and their soldiers on the day of the crucifixion of our God, because at His death and descent into Hades He did to them what He did to Pharaoh and the Egyptians, and freed the children of Adam from their prison as He freed the children of Israel from the land of Egypt.

St. Ambrose * Despite (the devil's) much boasting in speech and his insolence, the Savior seized him with a hook like a great dragon (Job 41:1), and like a beast the bridle was put in his jaws, and like a fugitive He bound his nostril with a rope, and pierced his lips with a thorn (Job 41:2); the Lord bound him like a bird that we might mock him (Job 41:5), and with him the demons his companions, like serpents and scorpions (Lk 10:19), that we might crush them and tread them under our feet.
Pope Athanasius the Apostolic Canst thou put a rope into his snout? or bore his jaw through with a hook? [2]

"Canst thou put a rope into his snout": the Septuagint reads: [Wilt thou put a ring in his nostrils?]. Pope Gregory (the Great) holds that his two nostrils refer to his deceitfulness, while the ring refers to the omnipotence of the divine power.

If the enemy of good does not cease to breathe out his deceptions and wiles as with his nose, so that man may fall into a chain of sins, and despair comes upon him and he does not rise, the mighty mercies of God nullify these deceptions, and man is filled with hope of forgiveness of his sins, and rises by the grace of God working in him.

Some hold that he is speaking here about the ornaments with which the Egyptians adorned the crocodile as a god. But it is clear that the talk here is not about deifying the crocodile and adorning it, but about its violence and the impossibility of taming it.

Rope (agmon): the exact translation means a kind of cord. It is as if he meant here that Leviathan has a marvelous strength, so that it is impossible to put a cord around his ear to bind his jaws. It was the custom in the East to put a ring in the ear of bulls and buffaloes and lead them by it.

Hook (choach): it is in truth a ring. It was, and still is, the custom to put a strong iron ring in the jaw of a large fish when it is caught, and the fisherman ties a cord to the ring and leaves the fish in the water, to draw it out when he finds someone to buy it.
Will he make many supplications unto thee? will he speak soft words unto thee? [3]

When a man falls into captivity he is crushed and humbles himself, but not so the enemy of good, who does not surrender or humble himself with many entreaties, for he does not submit quickly. He is like a beast of prey which, even after being caught, does not calm down but hopes to devour the one who caught it. The enemy of good is fierce and does not know the language of tenderness.

* If these words are addressed to the person of the Son, then (Satan) speaks soft words addressed to the Incarnate One, saying: "I know thee who thou art; the Holy One of God" (Lk 4:34). This leviathan makes many supplications to Him when it was said to Him by Legion: "If thou cast us out, suffer us to go away into the herd of swine" (Mt 8:31).
Pope Gregory (the Great)
* Satan is always diligent, even when danger comes upon him of losing his prey.
* Why does he return to attack? What do we learn from this? For even if we fall a thousand times, Satan will not stop, but continues the war without any hesitation.

* Observe that he goes about the world at every moment. Zechariah teaches us that the angels walk to and fro through the earth (Zech 1:10-11). But this wretch is not content with going about, for divine providence also does this work; he goes about in order to be condemned the more (for his evils), and that we may be the more on our guard. For this reason he was called [the ruler of the darkness of this world] (Eph 6:12); that is, the prince of evil.
Speak, O Satan, what have you done? He says: I have gone to and fro in the earth, I have walked up and down in it, and here I am.
What did he bring? He brought nothing useful or good, and so he did not answer why he went about.

St. John Chrysostom If the enemy of good does not know submission, he will not rest from resisting, even if he is overcome once and many times. But the Lord Christ cast out demons from many, and in humiliation the demons sometimes confessed Him as the Holy One of God, lest He torment them, and sometimes asked that He permit them to enter into the swine, as they said: Why art thou come to torment us? So he who bears the Lord Christ within him, the demons are confounded before him, as if they were entreating him to cease fighting them by his prayers and his deep communion with the Savior.

When we make a renewed practical covenant with God, the enemy of good collapses, for the believers are freed from the covenant which they had previously made with him. And, marvelously, instead of their being slaves of the devil, he becomes a slave to them, so that even if he breathes out his poisons, his wiles and his deception against them, all this is turned into their edification, their approval and their glorification.

* Through the sufferings the Lord ascended on high and led captivity captive, and gave gifts unto men (Ps 68:18; Eph 4:8), and gave to those who believe in Him authority to tread on serpents and scorpions and all the power of the enemy, that is, authority over the leader of the apostasy.

St. Irenaeus * Here protective care goes hand in hand with permission to strike, and the divine plan is fulfilled through protection and through the forsaking of the chosen servant, for while He forsakes him He guards him... So the saint was delivered into the hand of the adversary (Job 2:6), but his soul was kept in the hand of (God) his helper, for he was among the flock of whom the Truth says in the Gospel: "Neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand" (Jn 10:28).

Moreover, they do not see Lucifer rising, he of whom Isaiah said: [Lucifer, which shone in the morning], and then goes on: [cut down to the ground] (Isa 14:12), indicating that he does not regain his former honor. By his fall from heaven to earth he wanted the destruction of man, but God gives the one who is not deceived authority to tread the traitor under his feet and shatter him to pieces.
Abba Hesychius of Jerusalem Will he make a covenant with thee? wilt thou take him for a servant for ever? [4]
It refers to the animal mentioned: even if it falls into the snare it will not enter into a covenant with man, nor accept to serve him as a slave; it cannot be tamed.

We often think that we are strong, that sin will not harm us and the enemy cannot deceive us, so we are lax with sin and open the door to the enemy of good, thinking that he is enslaved and can serve us.

Eve opened the door to Leviathan, and entered into a dialogue with the serpent, and wished to establish a covenant, she and her husband and her offspring, with the devil and his hosts. She thought that the enemy would serve her, as he showed her the way to enjoy divinity and knowledge, and she fell into the humiliation of slavery to him. Dialogue with the enemy of good and entering into covenants with him will not avail, but leads us down to eternal destruction.

The devil made many offers to the Lord Christ during the temptation on the mountain, and when He rejected all his offers, "the devil leaveth him, and, behold, angels came and ministered unto him" (Mt 4:11).

* You are not the only one who does evil, but there is one who pushes you to it violently. He is Satan, who suggests evil to you without having compulsory mastery over the one who accepts it. Therefore the Preacher says: "If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, leave not thy place."

Close your door and drive him far from you, so that he does no harm to you; but if you accept the thought of lust without care, its roots will penetrate you, and your mind will be seduced by his wiles, and he will plunge you into the abyss of evils.
You may say: I am a believer; lust cannot come up upon me even if I think about it much!

Do you not know that the trunk of a tree, by continual resistance, can break even a rock?! So do not allow the seed to be found in you, lest it tear your faith apart and shatter it. Uproot evil by its root before it blossoms, lest through your negligence at the beginning you need axes and fire afterwards.
Treat your eyes in due time when they become inflamed, lest you become blind and need a physician!
St. Cyril of Jerusalem Wilt thou play with him as with a bird? or wilt thou bind him for thy maidens? [5]

A tamed bird can be played with for amusement and entertainment, but it is not so with Leviathan. For amusement birds are caught and put in cages so that young girls may stand around them enjoying the sight of them. In some undeveloped countries fathers tie birds with a string so that their children may play with them as a kind of amusement.

The enemy of good thinks of himself that he is the prince of this world, that no one has authority over him, and he did not realize that when the incarnate Word offered Himself as a sacrifice for the whole world, he lost his kingdom and became like a captive with no power or strength, whom little children courageously drag to trample him under their feet.

God raises up from the believers the army of spiritual salvation, which has no enemy but the devil and his angels. He trains His believers in spiritual combat, and gives even little children the possibility of victory, so that it is said of the Church, which was like dry bones cast in the midst of a valley: "The breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army" (Ezek 37:10); as it is also said of her: "Awesome as Jerusalem, as an army with banners" (Song 6:4).

Pope Gregory (the Great) holds that Satan, in his deception, uses every means to deceive man: he appears as the one who eats grass like the ox, as if he were a four-footed animal; again he appears as Leviathan in the waters, caught with a hook; and finally he appears as a bird in the air. He pursues man wherever he is, whether on land, or in the sea, or flying in the air. He is in the stupidity of animals despite his dangerous, deadly and attractive wiles, but in stupidity he lost his glory and his eternity; and he is wicked like the dragon in the sea, who does not cease to harm by every means, and he is proud, his heart is lifted up and he exalts himself like one who flies on high.
* Surely the Lord played with him as with a bird when He showed him the bait in the sufferings of the only-begotten Son of God, but He caught him in the net.
Pope Gregory (the Great)
* We find in Job this creature being played with by the heavenly angels, and the Lord gave His disciples authority to tread on serpents and scorpions and all the power of the enemy.

Theodoret of Cyrus * We look in amazement at His boundless and unutterable love, His infinite longsuffering, and His forgiveness at every moment of our sins which we confess to Him without measure, and His calling us despite our former unworthiness, but by His grace and mercy. Also the opportunities of salvation which He offers us without limit, giving us adoption, caring for us from childhood with grace and the knowledge of His laws. And He granted us to overcome by Him the enemy (Satan) through His good will in us, offering us eternal happiness and unfading crowns. Likewise His undertaking the economy of the Incarnation for our salvation and the breadth of the wonders of His mysteries which He offers to all the Gentiles.

Abba Moses * In ordinary battles the commanders do not arm women or children or old men, but our Commander, the Lord Christ, distributes this royal weapon (which is the possession of Christ Himself) to all equally. Then He teaches them the military stratagems of the devil.
Abba Theodoret * Follow the heavenly Bridegroom, that you may stand firm against the invisible enemies.

Wage war against principalities and powers (Eph 6:12), and first draw them away from yourself, so that they have no portion in you, and afterward drive them away from those who flee to you seeking protection through your counsel.
Cast them down under your feet as their leader and defender.
Do you renounce those disputations that are against the faith in Christ?

Fight with the word of godliness against the wicked, evil counsel. As the Apostle says: "Casting down imaginations, and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God" (2 Cor 10:5). Put your trust above all in the arm of the great King, at the mere sight of whom His enemies fear and tremble.
St. Basil the Great Shall the company of fishers dig a pit for him? or shall they part him among the Canaanites? [6]

Since Leviathan was a source of terror and represented a great danger, the fishermen did not care to catch him by any means, for the troubles of catching him do not equal their gains if they divide him among the merchants.
By the company here is meant the company of fishermen who join together to catch him in a net or a certain snare.
"Or shall they part him among the Canaanites?" The Septuagint reads: "Do the Gentiles feed on him?" and the Vulgate: "Do friends cut him up?"
The Canaanites were known as merchants; will they then divide him into parts, to sell him?
Canst thou fill his skin with barbed irons? or his head with fish spears? [7]

Large fish are usually caught with spears, but it is hard to catch the crocodile with spears, because it cannot be wounded by a spear unless it strikes him in the belly, which is hard to reach. For his back is covered with very strong scales which the spear cannot pierce.

Here he alludes to an instrument representing a spear in the shape of a fish with two tongues, often found engraved on Egyptian monuments. This spear was a slender rod ten to twelve feet long, with double feathers at the end like the modern arrow. It had two sharp ends about two feet long, encircled by a fish. The fisherman pushes it in the Nile, in a flat boat among the papyrus reeds and lotus plants, when he sees his prey with fins, and he draws the instrument with his right hand and moves it in the form of a bow with his left hand.
Lay thine hand upon him.
Remember the battle no more! [8]

The blessed Job, however great his righteousness, must remember the battle that took place between him (in the person of his parents Adam and Eve and their offspring) and Satan, for because of its bitterness man does not try to enter again into a battle with this crocodile. He says to him: Touch him if you dare. Good, but remember the previous battle before you begin trying to undertake a new battle, otherwise the results will be dire.

* The holy Job prophesied of the coming of the Lord, of whom he truly said that He would defeat the great leviathan (Job 41:8), and it has happened! For He struck the terrible leviathan, Satan, and cast him down, and humbled him in the last times by the honored sufferings of His body.
St. Ambrose God warns the blessed Job against entering into a battle with the devil by his own strength, thinking that he is able to lay his hand upon him, that is, to dominate him and overcome him.

* What if the Almighty God lightened the burdens we bear, but withdrew His help from us and left us amid the trials of this leviathan? Where shall we go when a strong enemy rises up against us, if we find no shelter in any protection of our Creator?

If you see the sword of the adversary attacking you, do not tremble at the blows of a father to you. For you see the blows with which I strike you, but you do not perceive the danger of the enemy from whom I free you by means of my blows to you... Therefore keep silence more and more while you are under the discipline of a father, and you will see the more that you are weak in regard to the attacks of the enemy. When you are struck by my correction of you, that you may acquire patience while you bear it, remember your enemy and do not count what you suffer as hard, for through the outward sufferings you are freed from the inward sufferings.
Pope Gregory (the Great)
Behold, the hope of him is in vain.
Shall not one be cast down even at the sight of him? [9]

There is no hope of overcoming him, for it is a vain hope. As soon as man looks upon this enemy he falls. The mere looking at him takes away man's hope and courage. This is what happens when one looks at the crocodile.

* Victory is not achieved by the amount of money, nor by pride in strength, nor by loftiness of glory, but the Lord gives His help freely to those who seek it with intense sorrows. So it was with Paul, who made his sorrows the object of his boasting. Therefore he was able to say: "When I am weak, then am I strong"...
Do you see where sorrows lead you? To the hope that maketh not ashamed (Rom 5:3).

St. Basil the Great * Let us not allow despair to possess us, for we have many incentives in good hope. Even if we sin every day, let us draw near to Him, entreating and supplicating, asking forgiveness of our sins, for in this way we draw further from sin, the nearer the time to come, and so we drive away Satan, and call upon the love and compassion of God, and receive the blessings of the age to come by the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ and His love for mankind.
St. John Chrysostom None is so fierce that dare stir him up: who then is able to stand before me? [10]

There is no wise man who would provoke the crocodile, or enter into a battle with him; how then can anyone stand before God Himself as an adversary and resist His plan, His judgments and His wisdom? If this is the position with a creature that God brought into being to be under the feet of man, to whom God gave authority over creation, how can man take a stand of rebellion against his Creator? Who can stand before God in His wrath?

*By the strong man is meant Satan, and his house is nothing but his kingdom on earth, while his goods are those people who imitate the devil their father in their affairs and works. Just as we call the saints holy vessels and consecrated goods, so the wicked may be called the goods and vessels of the devil, for they share with him in wickedness and evil. Christ the Word alone entered the house of the devil, this earthly world, and bound Satan in [chains of darkness and cast him down] (2 Pet 2:4). Levi was saved and was no longer a captive in the kingdom of Satan, and by his repentance became worthy of divine blessings, so we learn that repentance is the right way to salvation and redemption, for it was said: "Look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth" (Isa 45:22).

*It is enough for you what Habakkuk pointed out as he denounced the enemies of the Apostles: "Woe to him that increaseth that which is not his, and to him that ladeth himself with pledges! Shall they not rise up suddenly that bite thee, and awake that vex thee, and thou shalt be for booties unto them?" (Hab 2:6-7). For Satan has gathered into his fold all the inhabitants of the earth, who are not his, and made them bow down to him and worship him, and so he became burdened and magnified; but some awoke to despoil him of his spoils, for the Apostles cast the net of their teaching upon the captives and sinners, and returned with it to God filled with the people of the whole world.

St. Cyril the Great * [He shall judge the poor of the people, he shall save the children of the needy, and shall break in pieces the false accuser] (Ps 72:4). Rightly is Satan called "the false accuser," for he slandered God, and because of envy claimed that God had forbidden eating from the tree (of the knowledge of good and evil), and he slandered Job with lies, saying: "Doth Job fear God for nought?... Put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face" (Job 1:9, 11). In the eighth psalm he gave him the two names "the enemy and the avenger," while here (Ps 72:4) he calls him a false accuser.
Theodoret of Cyrus

11 "Who hath prevented me, that I should repay him? whatsoever is under the whole heaven is mine. 12 I will not conceal his parts, nor his power, nor his comely proportion. 13 Who can discover the face of his garment? or who can come to him with his double bridle? 14 Who can open the doors of his face? his teeth are terrible round about. 15 His scales are his pride, shut up together as with a close seal. 16 One is so near to another, that no air can come between them. 17 They are joined one to another, they stick together, that they cannot be sundered. 18 By his neesings a light doth shine, and his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning. 19 Out of his mouth go burning lamps, and sparks of fire leap out. 20 Out of his nostrils goeth smoke, as out of a seething pot or caldron. 21 His breath kindleth coals, and a flame goeth out of his mouth. 22 In his neck remaineth strength, and sorrow is turned into joy before him. 23 The flakes of his flesh are joined together: they are firm in themselves; they cannot be moved. 24 His heart is as firm as a stone; yea, as hard as a piece of the nether millstone. 25 When he raiseth up himself, the mighty are afraid: by reason of breakings they purify themselves. 26 The sword of him that layeth at him cannot hold: the spear, the dart, nor the habergeon. 27 He esteemeth iron as straw, and brass as rotten wood. 28 The arrow cannot make him flee: slingstones are turned with him into stubble. 29 Darts are counted as stubble: he laugheth at the shaking of a spear. 30 Sharp stones are under him: he spreadeth sharp pointed things upon the mire. 31 He maketh the deep to boil like a pot: he maketh the sea like a pot of ointment. 32 He maketh a path to shine after him; one would think the deep to be hoary. 33 Upon earth there is not his like, who is made without fear. 34 He beholdeth all high things: he is a king over all the children of pride."
Who hath prevented me, that I should repay him?
Whatsoever is under the whole heaven is mine [11].
Some hold that the expression here means: "Who does a kindness, that I may return it to him?"

Others hold that he means: who can foretell what will happen? If man cannot foretell what will happen when he is hunting a predatory beast, how then does he think he is able to subdue the Creator Himself, or to repay Him for His kindnesses? Who thinks that he is able to give me anything, when I am the owner of everything? It is fitting for man to submit to the Creator, and to accept everything with thanksgiving.
I will not conceal his parts, nor his power, nor his comely proportion [12].

Here He begins to give a detailed description of Leviathan, about whom He had already spoken in this chapter in general terms. He says: I cannot keep silent about speaking of his mouth and his teeth and his scales and the eyelids of his eyes and the openings of his nose, and his neck, and his heart.

The animal referred to here is not described to bring out its beauty, but as one who has great power and is exceedingly fierce: "his power, and his comely proportion (grace) of his armor," or the beauty of his weapons. The subject of His discourse is not the beauty of the animal, but its weapons of defense.
Who can discover the face of his garment? or who can come to him with his double bridle? [13]

No one can discover the face of his garment or his covering, that is, take off his hard, deceitful garment, to see his inner skin, nor can anyone dare to put a bridle on his jaws, as is done with other animals when they are bridled. It is not possible for anyone to dare to bring a double bridle to restrain the two rows of his teeth.

* This leviathan tempts the minds of the religious in one way, and the minds of those who are devoted to this world in another. For he openly presents to the wicked the evils they desire, but he secretly casts snares for the good, and deceives them under the appearance of holiness... Therefore the Apostle Paul, seeing some devoting themselves to the service of their bellies under the cloak of preaching, says: "For Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light. Therefore it is no great thing if his ministers also be transformed as the ministers of righteousness" (2 Cor 11:14-15). Joshua feared this transformation when he saw an angel and asked him on which side he was, saying: "Art thou for us, or for our adversaries?" (Josh 5:13).
Pope Gregory (the Great)
Who can open the doors of his face?
His teeth are terrible round about [14].
He calls his mouth "the doors of his face," for it is like a gate with two leaves.

This applies more to the crocodile, for Bochait says that the teeth of the crocodile number thirty, which is a large number, and their sizes are large compared with the size of its body; some of them protrude outside, and some are serrated like a saw, so that when it seizes its prey it cannot escape from it.
The Septuagint reads: "Who shall open the doors of his face?"

* [The doors of his face] are the wicked teachers, who are called the gates of his face, for everyone enters through them so that this leviathan is seen as if he were in his royal power... For when their vain preaching is accepted, the door of destruction opens for the wretched hearers.
Pope Gregory (the Great)
His scales are his pride, shut up together as with a close seal [15].
Rows of his scales cover him like shields; his body includes 17 rows, and there is no possibility of piercing his body except through his eyes or his throat (when he opens his mouth), or his belly.
Umbreit and Prof. Lee hold that the word "his pride" here in the original Hebrew is geewoh, which is like gewah or gevah, meaning a back, since the crocodile's back is covered with scales.
When the crocodile closes its mouth it becomes as if sealed with wax, so that no air leaks out from between its jaws and between its teeth.

*Satan is hard and without pity, and in his depths he never rests, for Holy Scripture says of him: [His heart is hard as a stone, and he stands like the hard anvil of a smith] (Job 41:24) LXX. But the saints have trampled him under their feet by the power of Christ, for He said: "Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall by any means hurt you" (Lk 10:19). Therefore Christ says: "Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat: but I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not."
St. Cyril the Great One is so near to another, that no air can come between them [16].
They are joined one to another, they stick together (are congealed), that they cannot be sundered [17].

* The scales of sinners are hard and bound together, so that it seems that no breath of life can pierce the mouth of the preachers. For those who practice similar sins gather together, in an evil defense, and become together in an obstinate agreement, so that each protects the other with a common defense of their sins. For each is afraid for himself when he sees another being rebuked or corrected... And while they protect one another in fellowship in their evils by their wicked motive, they do not allow the breath of holy counsel to reach them by any means... Union strengthens perversion, and makes them even more incorrigible, and so they become united together in unanimity.
Pope Gregory (the Great)
By his neesings a light doth shine, and his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning [18].

Amphibious animals dive into the water and hold their breath for a long time and then suddenly breathe out forcefully, so that it is as if they were sneezing, while they turn their eyes toward the sun so that they seem as if radiating fire, or they expel their breath so that it appears as if it were sunbeams.

[The eyelids (lids) of the morning]: the Egyptians depict the eyes of the crocodile as protruding forward as if they signified the early morning. When the crocodile rises to the surface, the first thing that appears of it is its eyes, before its whole body, so that it is like the appearance of the morning.

Some hold that since the crocodile remains under the water a long time, it rises to the surface to expel the water with a strong rush from the two openings of its nose, so that it appears like a rainbow.
When the crocodile is in the water its eyes appear dim or dull, but when it rises toward the surface they appear very bright.

* Anthony said: The demons often appear in this manner, as the Lord revealed to Job, saying: [His eyes are like the eyelids of the morning. Out of his mouth go burning lamps, and sparks of fire leap out. Out of his nostrils goeth smoke, as out of a seething pot or caldron. His breath kindleth coals, and a flame goeth out of his mouth] (Job 41:18-21). So the chief of the demons appears, as I said before, terrifying, and speaking with boasting and arrogance, as the Lord condemned him when He said to Job: "He esteemeth iron as straw, and brass as rotten wood" (Job 41:27). [He esteemeth the sea as a bath of water, and the bottom of the abyss as his captive, and the deep as a path for him] (Job 41:31-32). And as He said through a prophet: [The enemy said, I will pursue, I will overtake] (Ex 15:9). And He said through another prophet: [I will seize the whole world in my hand like a nest, and I will lift it up as one lifts abandoned eggs] (Isa 10:14). These things the demons boast of, and promise them to those who fear God in order to deceive them. Therefore it is fitting for us who are believers not to fear the appearances (of the devil) nor to heed his words, for he is a liar and never speaks the truth.
St. Athanasius the Apostolic Out of his mouth go burning lamps.
Sparks of fire leap out [19].

The animal is described here as one who vomits fire, for when it opens its mouth and its fangs appear, it emits fire upon those around it. Or like one who breathes and sends out violent fiery breaths that kill the prey and burn it.
* The lamps proceed from his mouth, for (the wicked teachers) kindle the minds of their hearers with the love of erroneous opinions, and while they seem to shine with wisdom, they burn with evil.
Pope Gregory (the Great)
Out of his nostrils goeth smoke, as out of a seething pot or caldron [20].
This simile applies to the horse used in battles, which sends out from its nostrils the smoke of burning fire.

* The dense breath of leviathan comes out of the two openings of his nose, for the evil of his pride issues forcefully from the puffs of his manifest wickedness... The smoke is said to come out of the two openings of the nose, by the deception of his miracles, which for a moment begets doubt even in the hearts of the elect. Smoke goes out of the mouth of leviathan because of false wonders, so that there is a threatening mist that corrupts the eyes even of those of good minds.
Pope Gregory (the Great)
His breath kindleth coals, and a flame goeth out of his mouth [21].
The same poetic description is used when speaking of the wrath of God (Ps 18:8).

* What is this that he calls coals but the minds of corrupt men, kindled with earthly passions? They are on fire when they seek any temporal thing, surely because their longings, which do not allow their minds to be calm and balanced, inflame them. The breath of leviathan kindles the coals when his secret suggestions strengthen the minds of men toward evil pleasures.

His breath has kindled some with the torches of pride, others with envy, others with lust, and others with covetousness. He kindled the torch of pride in the mind of Eve, when he suggested to her that she should make light of the words of the Lord's commandment. And he set the mind of Cain on fire with the flame of envy when he was grieved at the acceptance of his brother's sacrifice, until he reached the sin of murdering his brother. He set the heart of Solomon on fire with the torches of lust, he whom he overcame by the love of women, and they led him to idolatry, and he forgot to give due honor to his Creator when the pleasures of the flesh drew him. He also inflamed the mind of Ahab with the love of covetousness when he urged him, in haste, to seek another's vineyard, and this drove him to the crime of murder.
The flame of the mouth is truly the very making of a secret suggestion.
Pope Gregory (the Great)
In his neck remaineth strength, and sorrow is turned into joy before him [22].

"In his neck remaineth strength," that is, strength dwells there continually. While strength rests around his neck, since he breathes out terror, terror rejoices and dances with delight before him, spreading trembling upon those around him.

* We understand from these words that there is one King, who is the Creator of the whole universe. On the other side there is the prince of this world, who calls himself the king of darkness. Myriads of angels serve the true King, while myriads of demons surround the prince of the powers of darkness (Col 1:13). The principalities and powers and virtue follow the King of kings and Lord of lords. And in the end, when Christ delivers up the kingdom to God the Father, after He has put down all rule and all authority and power of the enemy, it is necessary that He reign till He has put all enemies under His feet (1 Cor 15:24-25).

St. Gregory of Nyssa * What does the neck of this leviathan mean but the stretching out of his pride, whereby he exalts himself against God, while pretending holiness, as he is puffed up with the pride of authority? The prophet Isaiah bears witness to this pride, expressed by the neck, when he rebuked the daughters of Jerusalem, saying: "They walk with stretched forth necks" (Isa 3:16). It is said that strength remains (abides) in the neck of this leviathan, and because of the authority that has been added to his pride. For he continues his exalted pride and all his wicked plans by the power of his temporal authority.
Pope Gregory (the Great)

* By such words (Jn 12:31; 14:30; 16:11) He refers to Satan as a prince not over God's creatures, but over sinners, those whom He here indicates by the name "this world." When He uses the name "world" in the sense of evil, the Lord refers only to the lovers of this world, of whom it is written elsewhere: [The friendship of the world is enmity with God] (Jas 4:4). Far be it from us to understand Satan as the prince of the world in the sense of one who controls the management of the affairs of the whole world, heaven and earth and all that is in them. Of such a world it was said when we spoke of Christ the Word: "The world was made by him" (Jn 1:10). The whole world, from the highest heavens to the lowest parts of the earth, is subject to the Creator, not to the fugitive; to the Savior, not to the destroyer; to the Deliverer, not to the enslaver; to the Teacher, not to the deceiver.

*But the prince of this world (Satan), who rules wherever there is error and confusion, departs from a man whose life is ruled by peace and perfect order, and over whom the Son of God has dominion. When this peace arises from within and is established, all the persecutions that the prince of this world stirs up from without cannot shake anything of that inner building; rather, the strength of the building from within causes the plots of the devil from without to fail. Therefore the Lord went on to say: "Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness' sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven."

* "For either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon." Whoever serves mammon serves Satan, whom our Lord called (the prince of this world), because of his dominion by his error over earthly things. So a man will either "hate" this one "and love the other," that is, God, or hold to the one, "Satan," and despise the other, "God." For he who serves mammon is subject to the cruel and destructive Satan. For when he is entangled by his lust for money he submits to Satan and clings to him though he does not love him, for who among us loves Satan?! And so he is like a man who loved a maidservant of a great person, and though he does not love her master he submits to his cruel slavery because of his love for the maidservant.
St. Augustine The flakes of his flesh are joined together: they are firm in themselves; they cannot be moved [23].
Usually the layers of flesh at the neck and at the belly are soft and weak, but in this animal the layers of flesh at his neck are joined together, molded as of iron, strong.

What a hideous picture! Just as the body of Christ grows to include every day souls that enjoy the righteousness and holiness of Christ and become partners with Him in glory, so also the body of the devil grows to include those who are more wicked than the former, and all are joined together like the joined flakes of the devil's flesh, as if they had become one mass like iron molded together, unmoved toward repentance and return to God. The union of the wicked together corrupts souls, and shuts the door before many from thinking seriously about enjoying the divine truth.

If the Lord Christ has joined us to Himself to be members of His one body, by our enjoying faith in Him, and our being born of the Spirit as children of God in the waters of Baptism, our mission is to join together in love every day those who are saved and who enjoy with us fellowship with Him in the new risen life which He gave us. So also the flakes of the body of Satan are those who have accepted sonship to him and are united with him through his works, and they do not cease to draw many with them to be members in the body of the devil, sharing his final fate even more than they do; for the wicked man is pleased when he joins with him one who becomes more wicked than himself.

* The body of leviathan (the wicked indeed) is wholly corrupt, for they have no longing for their spiritual city. The flakes of the body of leviathan are those who join these persons in a wicked life, and even outstrip the former in the way of evil... In the wicked company of this leviathan, these are the members of his body who by their wicked deeds join to him those whom they make more wicked than themselves.
Pope Gregory (the Great)
His heart is as firm as a stone; yea, as hard as a piece of the nether millstone [24].

The Lord Christ says: "God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham" (Mt 3:9). What are these stones that give children to Abraham but the idolaters, who worship stone, and the sons of the devil who bear his hard, stony heart (Job 41:24), that they may become children of God bearing the faith of Abraham.

Some hold that the huge predatory animals have weak feelings and a hard heart, if the expression is right, and care nothing for the cries of the prey and the blood shed from it while it is between their fangs.
He chooses here the lower millstone, because it must be harder and heavier than the upper stone, so that it may bear the motion of the upper stone and its pressure upon it.

Perhaps some will ask: Is Satan not given the joy of repenting? Since his fall he has not only been determined to resist God, but has increased in violence in his attitude, and even stirs up mankind to be like him, and to share in his violence and hardness of heart; so with time the cup of his evil is filled the more, and he cares nothing for eternal punishment, but finds his pleasure in the children of men sharing this fate with him.
* The heart of the ancient enemy will remain like a stone, for it will not be softened by any remorse of repentance. It will only be prepared for the blasts of eternal punishment.
Pope Gregory (the Great)

* He is violent, knows no pity, and cannot be calmed in heart. As Holy Scripture says of him: "His heart is hard as a stone, and he stands like an anvil that is not struck" (Job 41:24) LXX. But Christ puts him under the feet of the saints. He says: "Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall by any means hurt you" (Lk 10:19).

St. Cyril the Great * So also Satan transforms himself into the form of an angel of light (2 Cor 11:14), not in order to ascend again to where he was, for his heart is hard as an anvil, so that his will has become incapable of repenting. But he does this with the intention of plunging those who walk in an angelic life into the darkness of blindness and deadly unbelief.

Many wolves go about in sheep's clothing (Mt 7:15), yes, their clothes are sheep's clothing, but not their hooves or their teeth. And as they walk in the soft skin they deceive the innocent by their appearance, and pour into them from their fangs the poison of deadly defilement.

St. Cyril of Jerusalem * I will declare with confidence that there is one who is not much affected by [the hammer of the whole earth]. And since the example has been given of a hammer that can be perceived, look for a material stronger than the hammer which is not affected by its blows. By searching for it I found it in what is written: "Behold a man standing upon walls of adamant" (adamant: a hard stone which was thought to be uncuttable, and some thought it to be the diamond). History records of adamant that it is stronger than every hammer that strikes it, for it will neither break nor yield. Even if the hammer is the devil who stands upon it, and the serpent who with his unconquerable anvil places it under him, yet the adamant is not affected at all when it rests in the hand of God and under His care. Thus those who oppose the adamant are the hammer and the immovable anvil. However, there is in truth a very common proverb among the Gentiles in the common language concerning those who suffer from troubles and very difficult circumstances. They say: They are between the hammer and the anvil. Yet it can be said that this refers to Satan and the serpent, who are always meant by such two names in the Holy Scriptures for different purposes. And you can say that the holy person who is an adamant wall, or who is an adamant in the hand of the Lord, is affected neither by the hammer nor by the anvil, but the more he is struck the more the brightness of his shining virtue increases.

* He says: "Thus he shewed me: and, behold, the Lord stood upon a wall of adamant, and in his hand was an adamant" (Amos 7:7) LXX. If Satan is a hard hammer from above and the dragon like the hard anvil (Job 41:15) stands from below, then he who is in the hand of the Lord and under His protection is hard and never yields. For the holy man is an adamant wall, and as he remains in the hands of the Lord he suffers nothing even if he is placed between the hammer (the devil) and the dragon (the anvil). And the more the blows fall upon him, the more his virtue becomes bright. For Satan, being ignorant of this kind of rock (the adamant), wants to break it up by many blows like a hard hammer, but God alone knows their nature well.
Origen When he raiseth up himself, the mighty are afraid.
By reason of terrors they wander [25].

When he rises to attack or to defend himself, the mighty are terrified before him, and from fear their thoughts collapse and they wander, or lose the way. They try to flee from him and do not know where to go.
The sword of him that layeth at him cannot hold: the spear, the dart (javelin), nor the habergeon [26].
The sword cannot overtake him, for it cannot break his scales. And if spears are aimed at him they rebound without piercing his scales.

* The spear of holy preaching is gentle; when we are struck by it we die to sin. But the sword of the satanic call is wicked; by it a man is wounded with deadly wounds until he is deprived of uprightness of life...
Pope Gregory (the Great)
He esteemeth iron as straw, and brass as rotten wood [27].
By iron and brass he means the metal weapons used against him; they are like straw and wood and worms, without power.

What occupies the devil's mind is not his bitter fate, but how to draw the souls of men to evil, especially the souls of believers; if he sees a soul strong as iron and hard as brass, he directs the arrows of his evil until the iron is turned into straw (chaff), and the brass into a feeble piece of wood. The enemy concentrates his blows the more on the preachers and witnesses to the evangelical truth, and those who labor in the Lord's vineyard.

* When this leviathan takes that sword which the Holy Scriptures call "the antichrist" to practice his evil, he turns iron into straw and brass into wood, unless divine grace intervenes to give protection from him, lest he turn the strength of the preachers into straw and destroy them with the fire of his evil, and make them like dust by turning their patience into wood.
Pope Gregory (the Great)
The arrow cannot make him flee.
Slingstones are turned with him into stubble [28].

We can interpret this passage as relating to the believer: if the enemy of good spares no effort to urge believers to evil, and his battle against the Church of Christ never ceases, the believer for his part does not fear these satanic wars so long as he is sheltered by the Lord Christ, bearing the weapon of living faith. He is not terrified by the arrows of the devil's bow, nor by the stones, for the stones of his sling, which become like straw, will do him no harm.

* If you say that the opposing power is very strong, and that evil has complete mastery over man, you thereby attribute injustice to God when He condemns men for being subject to Satan, since Satan is very strong and subdues mankind with an irresistible power. By this you make Satan greater and stronger than the soul, and then you tell me not to submit to Satan. This is like a fight between a young man and a little child, in which the child, when defeated, is condemned for his defeat. This is a great injustice!

St. Macarius the Great * Do not fear Satan, then, even though he is without a body, when he approaches the body. For there is none weaker than he who approaches in this way, although he is not clothed with a body, and none stronger than that bold, courageous man, even though he bears a mortal body!
St. John Chrysostom Darts are counted as stubble: he laugheth at the shaking of a spear [29].
No tool or weapon can wound the crocodile, nor can any human power overtake it.

Pope Gregory (the Great) holds that this passage applies to the devil, whom the Lord rebukes and reproves, as if he were being struck with a hammer; but in persistence in his evil he cares nothing for the blows of the hammer, but counts them as straw, and even laughs in mockery at these blows.

This applies also to the wicked who stubbornly hold to their evils, for God permits their chastening, that perhaps they may return to Him, but these blows with the hammer of chastening become to them like straw, and they do not return to the divine truth. Like their wicked master, the devil, they care nothing for the shaking of the divine spear to chasten them.

* The Lord shakes the spear against leviathan, for He threatens him with a harsh judgment for his destruction. For the shaking of the spear is the preparation of eternal death for him with a severe punishment. But the stubborn spirit, despising the Creator of life, even while he is threatened with his death laughs at Him who shakes the spear. Whatever his foreknowledge of his terrible, cruel fate drawing near to him with a firm sentence, he does not fear its coming upon him. Rather, the more he realizes that he is unable to escape the eternal torments, the more violently he increases in the practice of evil.
Pope Gregory (the Great)

Again, as this passage applies to the true believer, the enemy of good who wants to put him on the anvil and strike him with the hammer, shapes him according to his own desire; God does not restrain the hammer, and permits him to put him on the anvil, but the blows of the hammer are turned into worthless straw, with no effect on the mind and life of the believer.
God does not prevent the trials and allurements of Satan, but gives His believers strength, so the trials are turned to nothing, and the believer gains victory and a crown.
Sharp stones are under him.
He spreadeth sharp pointed things upon the mire [30].

Perhaps he refers here to sharp and hard scales like sharp pieces of potsherd. In some parts of the crocodile's body there are sharp scales, so that even when it rests on the mud found on the bank of the river it is like one resting on the teeth of a sharp threshing sledge. Perhaps he means that when it rests on sharp pieces of rock or jagged stones it feels no weariness or harm from them, but is as if it were resting on mud. Some scholars hold that when spears and other weapons are aimed around it they are broken and scattered around it, like sharp pieces of potsherd cast around it. Others hold that if this animal rests on mud, when it leaves the place it leaves the marks of its scales as if weapons had left their marks on the mud.
He maketh the deep to boil like a pot: he maketh the sea like a pot of ointment [31].

By his swift movement under the water he makes the river or the sea like a boiling pot. He makes the sea like a vessel containing perfumes; here is a reference to the smell of musk which, as they thought, comes from the crocodile. Some hold that when he moves vigorously in the depths of the sea he stirs up the mud in it, just as a man stirs a vessel of perfume so that the fragrance may be carried up from the sediment in the vessel.
The word "sea" here refers to the river Nile, because of its breadth, for to this day it is called in many regions of Upper Egypt "the sea." It applies also to the river Euphrates.

* What does he mean by the sea but the life of the lovers of the world, and what does he mean by the deep but their deep hidden thoughts? For this leviathan makes this deep sea boil like a pot, for it is very clear that in the last days of persecution he works to stir up the minds of the wicked against the elect with the flame of cruelty.

When ointments boil, a sweet fragrance comes from them. Leviathan will deceive the hearts of the wicked, so that whatever evil deeds of unbelief they do, they think they are doing them for the sake of truth and right faith.
Pope Gregory (the Great)

What a deception of the wicked enemy! He stirs up the wicked who are like the sea and takes control of their hidden thoughts to urge them to resist the children of God by every means, and when they kill them they think they are offering service to God, as the Lord Christ Himself said (Jn 16:2).

Their depths boil with evil, and they think they are offering the ointments of truth with its sweet fragrance, in contrast to what the Lord Christ, the Truth, offers in the life of His children, that they may say with the Apostle Paul: "For we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ" (2 Cor 2:15).
He maketh a path to shine after him; one would think the deep to be hoary [32].
Because of the swiftness of his movement he leaves behind him white foam, as happens when swift ships pass through the waters. His traces look like the hair of an old gray-haired man.

Just as the Lord Christ makes His true believers "the light of the world," shining by Him on those around them to bring them into the kingdom of light, so the enemy deceives his followers. He appears as an angel of light (2 Cor 11:14), and suggests to his followers that they know the truth and light the way, and that they have hidden wisdom, so that their bulk or their depths become like the gray-haired man of long experience and practical wisdom.

* Let no one be surprised at the heresies that exist today, for they have existed from the beginning, because Satan skillfully tries to mix falsehood with truth. And just as God from the beginning promised man many good things, so Satan always entices with his deceptive promises. God planted for them the garden of Eden, and Satan came and said to them: "Ye shall be as gods," and in fact he could not give them anything; all he did was dazzle them with his promises only. And this is what deceivers do.
St. John Chrysostom Upon earth there is not his like, who is made without fear [33].

In the Hebrew it reads "upon the mire." There is no animal like him, or the earth has not brought forth an animal so terrifying in its strength, violence, courage and ferocity. It is as if he were created so as not to fear or dread anyone.

Truly the devil has no equal on earth, and as Pope Gregory (the Great) says, although men know of his fall because of his deeds, yet he has not lost his angelic capabilities (his powers which he turned to evil), so he drew the human race and subjected it to himself. He boasts of the strength of his nature, by which he was able to rule over men.

* This is the enemy from whom we must flee. Who is this lion that follows us? St. Peter warns us and says to us: "Your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour: whom resist stedfast in the faith" (1 Pet 5:8-9).
So there is a lion that has come up from his thicket: where then is this thicket? He fell down. He went down to the lowest parts of the earth, to its depths.
You are a man, you are higher than Satan, for in any case you are better than he. But he, because of his corruption, has gone down to the depths.

So if this lion comes out of his thicket, that is, from the place of his punishment (Hades), it will be said: "The lion is come up from his thicket, and the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way; he is gone forth from his place to make thy land desolate" (Jer 4:7). He wants to enter your land, and wants to devour each one of us.

"Thy cities shall be laid waste, without an inhabitant. For this gird you with sackcloth" (b). Therefore, since the lion has come up to you to threaten you and to destroy your land, put on sackcloth, and weep and sigh and entreat God in prayers to destroy this lion and bring him to nothing so that you may be rid of him, and not fall between his teeth. For he tries to catch you through your ears, when he casts to you false words that are pleasing to your soul, to make you turn aside from the way of truth. And he wants also to devour your feet, and pull them away from the ground of truth. So be it! Gird yourself with sackcloth, and beat your breast, weep, and cry the cries of war when you see the enemy threatening you, that the fierceness of the Lord's anger may turn back from you, for you will have entered into the fortified city. Let us give thanks to God who delivers us in Christ Jesus, to whom be glory and might forever and ever, amen.
Origen He beholdeth all high things.
He is a king over all the children of pride [34].

He concludes his description by saying that in his arrogance he looks upon all the fierce and violent, haughty animals as less than himself, and oversees them as a king with authority; there is no animal that can resist him. All are subject to him, and he is subject to no one.

The lion is called the king of the forest or the king of the beasts; he is one of the children of pride, exalting himself by his power and capabilities. But before the animal mentioned here the lion loses his title.

* He looks down as one who is above all those who are beneath him. In his struggle against his Creator he disdains that anyone be reckoned like himself... In this it was well said by the prophet: "Woe unto them that are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight!" (Isa 5:21). So Paul says: "Be not wise in your own conceits" (Rom 12:16).

* "He is a king over all the children of pride." This leviathan, in order to fall in all the things mentioned before, struck himself with pride... He attacked the anointing of our immortality with the same weapon, as he destroyed his own blessed life. But God put this at the end of His discourse, for by pointing to the pride of this leviathan after mentioning all his evils, He indicates that it is the worst of all sins...
The man who exalts himself shamelessly in his mind, destruction quickly comes upon him. It is written: "Pride goeth before destruction" (Prov 16:18).
Pope Gregory (the Great)

* We have fallen under the authority of our enemies - that is, "the god of this world" and his helpers from the powers of evil. As a result there arose our need of redemption by Him who buys us, so that we may return from the state of estrangement from Him. Therefore our Savior gave His blood as a ransom for us.... And since "the forgiveness of sins," which follows redemption, becomes impossible before man is set free, we must first be freed from the authority of him who took us captive and kept us under his control, and be freed from beyond the reach of his hand, so that we may obtain forgiveness of our sins and healing from the wounds of sin, so that we may accomplish works of godliness and other virtues.
*And truly; but if we prefer lust to God, sin reigns over us, for the Apostle says: "Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body" (Rom 6:12).
So two kings strive to reign: sin or Satan reigns over the wicked, and righteousness or Christ reigns over the righteous.

Since the devil knew that Christ had come to seize his kingdom and subject to His power and authority those who had formerly been subject to the deceiver, he "shewed him all the kingdoms of the world" and all the inhabitants of the world; he showed Him how he reigns over one by lust, and over another by stinginess, over a third by love of vain glory, and takes others captive through the attraction of beauty... As if Satan were saying to Him: Do you want to reign over all creation?! And he showed Him the countless multitudes who are subject to him, and truly, if we accepted to know in simplicity our wretchedness and realize our calamity, we would find Satan reigning over most of the world; therefore the Lord calls him "the prince of this world" (Jn 12:31; 16:11). And when the devil says to Jesus: Do you see all the people subject to my authority? he has shown Him that "in a moment of time," for he reckons the present time a moment compared with eternity... Then the devil said to the Lord: Have you come to wrestle against me, and to take away from me all those who are under my authority? No, no, do not try to compare yourself with me, and do not expose yourself to the difficulties of this battle. See all that I ask of you, "If thou therefore wilt worship me, all shall be thine."
Without doubt our Lord and Savior wants to reign, but by justice and truth and every virtue... He does not want to be crowned as king without toil (the Cross)...

The Lord answered him, saying: [It is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve] (Deut 6:13) (c). My will is that all be Mine and worship Me, and not bow down to another. This is the royal desire. Would you have me sin, I who came to destroy sin and set men free from it?!
Let us rejoice and be glad, since we have become His, and let us pray to Him to kill the sin that reigned in our bodies (Rom 6:6), that He alone may reign over us.
Origen
By You I overcome him who overcame mankind!
* I have nothing to offer You but the sacrifice of praise, O Lover of all mankind!
You came into our world and clothed Yourself with our humanity, You became a true man, and the devil coveted You.
He thought You, like all men, would bow to him in humiliation.
* You offered him Your body as bait, and he leapt to devour it on the Cross.
The divine hook caught him, and he who thought himself king of the world became a plaything.
He fell into the snare, and his tongue was bound as with the cord of faith!
The little girls mocked him. He fell like lightning from the heaven of their hearts.
He was brought low to be under their feet.
He thought that by deceitful soft words he would escape from Your hand.
He confessed that You are the Holy One of God. And he realized that You had come to cast him out of his kingdom.
The enemy was confounded, but in his insolence he continued in his evil.
* By Your Cross You tore up my covenant with the enemy of good.
You freed me from him who thought he would enslave me eternally.
Instead of my humiliation before him, he has become humiliated. His resistance to me has not ceased, but it no longer crushes me. By You I overcome him who overcame mankind!
* I will no longer trust his promises.
I will not enter again into dialogue with him.
I will not waste my time with his words!
Your wonderful covenant with me is enough for me!
You gave it to me written with Your blood on the Cross.
* In his deceit he comes to me wherever I am.
On the land I see him eating grass like the ox.
And in the sea I see him swimming like the crocodile.
And in the air he appears like a bird soaring to the heights!
He uses every means to join me to himself.
He stirs up passions so that man may find pleasure in them.
And he breathes the spirit of pride to puff up the believer with his own righteousness.
He appears as a lion to terrify those who look at him.
And he appears as an angel of light to deceive the believers.
